1-chronicles-12:40:2.summary: Judah’s quarrel over eating at the king’s expense does not connect to the Hebron feast.

1-chronicles-12:40:3.summary: Jacob and his kinsmen “ate and drank” on the mountain, a covenant meal loosely like the Hebron feast.

1-chronicles-12:41:0.summary: Abigail loads donkeys with wine, raisins, and “fig cakes,” the same provisions brought for David.

1-chronicles-12:41:1.summary: Ziba brings donkeys with raisins and wine for David, similar provisions on pack animals.

1-chronicles-12:41:2.summary: A city prospering through the righteous loosely fits Israel’s gladness at David’s reign.

1-chronicles-12:41:3.summary: Peoples rejoice when the righteous are honored, loosely like Israel’s gladness.

1-chronicles-12:41:4.summary: Rejoicing because the Lord reigns broadly parallels gladness at David’s accession.

1-chronicles-12:41:5.summary: The people rejoice greatly when Solomon is made king, like Israel’s gladness for David.

1-chronicles-12:41:6.summary: The crowd rejoices at the coming King, a typological echo of joy at David’s reign.

1-chronicles-12:41:7.summary: The promised Davidic king brings security to Judah and Israel, loosely like the joy in Israel.

1-chronicles-12:41:8.summary: The people rejoice at a rightful king’s installation, a general parallel.

1-chronicles-12:41:9.summary: Supporters bring flour, sheep, and other provisions for David and his people, like the neighbors’ abundant supplies.

1-chronicles-12:18:7.summary: 1 Samuel 18:3 has no corresponding passage in this edition, which follows the Greek text; there is no Saints reading to compare.
1-chronicles-12:18:7.why: Compare a Hebrew-based translation if this passage matters for study.
1-chronicles-12:18:7.note: Passage unavailable in this edition; the review records the absence rather than an interpretation.

1-chronicles-12:18:10.summary: 1 Samuel 18:1 has no corresponding passage in this edition, which follows the Greek text; there is no Saints reading to compare.
1-chronicles-12:18:10.why: Compare a Hebrew-based translation if this passage matters for study.
1-chronicles-12:18:10.note: Passage unavailable in this edition; the review records the absence rather than an interpretation.

1-chronicles-13:1:0.summary: A king gathers rulers before acting for the Lord’s house, loosely like David consulting leaders.

1-chronicles-13:1:1.summary: Josiah gathers elders before religious reform, broadly like David consulting leaders.

1-chronicles-13:1:2.summary: The king gathers Judah’s elders, a general parallel to David’s consultation.

1-chronicles-13:1:3.summary: Both mention “leaders” of thousands, but in different episodes.

1-chronicles-13:1:4.summary: David gathers Israel’s chosen men to bring up the ark, Samuel’s parallel to this consultation.
1-chronicles-13:1:4.why: Parallel opening of the ark narrative.

1-chronicles-13:1:5.summary: Issachar’s men knew “what Israel should do,” loosely fitting David’s taking counsel.

1-chronicles-13:1:6.summary: Both mention army leaders over hundreds and thousands, but the Gaddite muster is a separate episode.

1-chronicles-13:2:0.summary: Israel’s defeat at Gelboue has no specific link to David’s call to gather the scattered brethren.

1-chronicles-13:2:1.summary: The Kohathites’ duties with the ark (truncated) give background for summoning priests and Levites.

1-chronicles-13:2:2.summary: Only the idea of those who “remain” overlaps; Hezekiah’s plea concerns Assyria.

1-chronicles-13:2:3.summary: The elders’ conditional counsel to Rehoboam is unrelated to David’s proposal.

1-chronicles-13:2:4.summary: Jehu’s conditional demand shares only an “if” clause with David’s proposal.

1-chronicles-13:2:5.summary: Proverbs praises taking counsel, loosely fitting David consulting the assembly.

1-chronicles-13:2:6.summary: David’s concern for the ark’s housing is a related but later initiative.

1-chronicles-13:2:7.summary: The Levites’ allotted towns explain the source’s “Levites, in their possession towns.”

1-chronicles-13:2:8.summary: Jethro’s “If you do this thing, God shall strengthen you” loosely resembles David’s conditional appeal.

1-chronicles-13:2:9.summary: Israel abandoning cities after Saul’s death is not the gathering David proposes.

1-chronicles-13:2:10.summary: Paul’s appeal in love is unrelated to David’s proposal to the assembly.

1-chronicles-13:2:11.summary: Hezekiah provides for priests and Levites (truncated), only generally related to summoning them.

1-chronicles-13:2:12.summary: David assembles all Israel and the Levites to bring up the ark, the completion of this plan.
1-chronicles-13:2:12.why: Shows the plan done properly later.

1-chronicles-13:2:13.summary: The list of Aaronic and Levitical dwelling places (truncated) identifies the towns the source mentions.

1-chronicles-13:3:0.summary: The ark sat in Kiriath-jearim for many years, explaining why it was not sought since Saul’s days.

1-chronicles-13:3:1.summary: David inquires of the Lord, a general theme of seeking God unlike Saul’s neglect.

1-chronicles-13:3:2.summary: A priest urges Saul to draw near to God, loosely reflecting how seeking God fared in Saul’s days.

1-chronicles-13:3:3.summary: In the Saints text Saul calls for the “ephoud,” not the ark, so the assumed ark link is absent.

1-chronicles-13:3:4.summary: Inquiring “through God” for David touches on seeking God, but not the ark.

1-chronicles-13:3:5.summary: The psalm recalls finding the ark “in the plains of the forest,” the Jarim setting from which David retrieves it.
1-chronicles-13:3:5.why: Poetic memory of recovering the ark.

1-chronicles-13:3:6.summary: Inquiring through God for David is a general theme of seeking God, not the ark.

1-chronicles-13:3:7.summary: David seeks God through the ephoud, a general contrast with the neglect under Saul.

1-chronicles-13:4:0.summary: “The proposal pleased the king and the assembly” matches the whole assembly agreeing that the matter was right.

1-chronicles-13:4:1.summary: Both use “right in his eyes,” but about Michal’s love for David.

1-chronicles-13:4:2.summary: Esther’s “If it seems good to you” echoes David’s preceding proposal more than the assembly’s agreement.

1-chronicles-13:4:3.summary: The people approve what the king does, a general parallel to the assembly’s agreement.

1-chronicles-13:5:0.summary: The ark was brought to Kiriath-jearim, the “city of Jarim” from which David fetches it.
1-chronicles-13:5:0.why: How the ark came to be there.

1-chronicles-13:5:2.summary: Both gather all Israel from “the entrance of Hamath/Emath” to Egypt’s border for a sacred occasion.
1-chronicles-13:5:2.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

1-chronicles-13:5:3.summary: “David assembled all Israel … to bring the Lord’s ark” repeats this verse’s wording for the second attempt.

1-chronicles-13:5:4.summary: Only the place name Aimath/Hamath overlaps; the candidate is the exile of Judah.

1-chronicles-13:5:5.summary: Both mention “Egypt’s borders” as the extent of Israel’s realm, under Solomon.

1-chronicles-13:5:6.summary: The land runs from Egypt to “the entrance of Hamath,” the same boundaries as David’s assembly.
1-chronicles-13:5:6.why: Ideal borders of the promised land.

1-chronicles-13:5:7.summary: The next verse continues the same event: all Israel going up to bring the ark.

1-chronicles-13:5:8.summary: The promised land’s borders run from Egypt’s wadi to “the entrance into Hamath,” matching the source.

1-chronicles-13:5:9.summary: Jeremiah’s rebuke about Egypt’s road shares only the name Egypt.

1-chronicles-13:6:0.summary: God speaks from “between the two cherubim upon the ark,” the basis for the ark being “enthroned upon cherubim.”

1-chronicles-13:6:2.summary: Hezekiah addresses the Lord “seated upon the cherubim,” the same title used of the ark here.

1-chronicles-13:6:3.summary: The candidate equates Baal with “the city of Jearim,” where the ark was, but the Saints source says the “City of David.”
1-chronicles-13:6:3.why: Greek wording obscures the place link.

1-chronicles-13:6:4.summary: “Kiriath-baal—that is the city of Jearim” identifies the ark’s location, though the Saints source names the City of David.
1-chronicles-13:6:4.why: Greek wording obscures the place link.

1-chronicles-13:6:5.summary: “The ark of the Lord, who is seated upon the cherubim” is carried out, the same title as here.
1-chronicles-13:6:5.why: Earlier ark movement with same title.

1-chronicles-13:6:6.summary: “He sits upon the cherubim” echoes the ark of the Lord “enthroned upon cherubim.”

1-chronicles-13:6:7.summary: Hezekiah’s prayer addresses God “seated upon the cherubim,” matching the source’s title.

1-chronicles-13:6:8.summary: “Thou who sittest upon the cherubim” uses the same divine title as the source.

1-chronicles-13:6:9.summary: God choosing a place for His name loosely echoes the ark “where His name was invoked.”

1-chronicles-13:6:10.summary: “Every place where I name My name” loosely echoes the ark “where His name was invoked.”

1-chronicles-13:6:11.summary: “My name is upon him” concerns the angel, only loosely like the name invoked over the ark.

1-chronicles-13:6:12.summary: Putting God’s name on Israel loosely resembles the name invoked over the ark.

1-chronicles-13:6:13.summary: God speaks from above the ark “between the two cherubim,” the presence behind the cherubim title.
1-chronicles-13:6:13.why: Ark as place of God’s presence.

1-chronicles-13:7:0.summary: The law has Kohathites carry the holy things without touching them, unlike the ark placed on a cart.

1-chronicles-13:7:1.summary: The ark was placed in “Aminadab’s house,” from which it is now taken on the cart.

1-chronicles-13:7:3.summary: David later admits God “cut among us” because they did not seek according to judgment, explaining this cart transport.

1-chronicles-13:7:4.summary: “No one may lift God’s ark except the Levites” corrects the cart method used here.

1-chronicles-13:7:5.summary: The Philistines also sent the ark on “a new cart,” the precedent David imitates.

1-chronicles-13:8:0.summary: Both list praise with trumpet, lyre, tambourine, and cymbals before God.

1-chronicles-13:8:2.summary: Levites praise with instruments David made, a general link to musical worship.

1-chronicles-13:8:3.summary: Trumpets and cymbals for God’s songs appear in later ark worship, sharing instruments with the source.

1-chronicles-13:8:4.summary: Elisha’s string player shares only music, not the ark procession.

1-chronicles-13:8:5.summary: The Levites prepare to bring up the ark properly (truncated), the corrected sequel to this procession.

1-chronicles-13:8:6.summary: Instruments summon worship of Nebuchadnezzar’s image, unrelated to the ark procession.

1-chronicles-13:8:7.summary: God ascending “with the sound of a trumpet” fits a procession theme but names no ark.

1-chronicles-13:8:8.summary: David appoints musicians with kinyrai, nablai, and cymbals, a later organization of worship music.

1-chronicles-13:8:9.summary: “All Israel brought up the ark” with trumpets, cymbals, harps, and lyres, the second procession’s parallel.

1-chronicles-13:8:10.summary: Asaph’s Levites play harps, lyres, and cymbals before the ark after its arrival.

1-chronicles-13:8:11.summary: Prophets with tambourine and lyres share instruments but not the ark event.

1-chronicles-13:8:12.summary: A sacred procession with musicians and tambourines loosely parallels the ark procession.

1-chronicles-13:8:13.summary: Amos condemns self-indulgent music, unrelated to playing before God.

1-chronicles-13:8:14.summary: God rejecting Israel’s songs and instruments has no specific link to David’s worship.

1-chronicles-13:10:0.summary: The Levites later carry the ark on poles as Moses commanded, the correct way that avoids Oza’s fate.

1-chronicles-13:10:1.summary: David says “our God cut among us” for not seeking according to judgment, referring to Oza’s death.

1-chronicles-13:10:2.summary: The law forbids touching the holy things “so that they do not die,” the rule Oza violated.

1-chronicles-13:10:3.summary: The Lord strikes the men of Beth-shemesh over the ark, a parallel judgment for mishandling it.

1-chronicles-13:10:4.summary: Paul links irreverence toward holy things to sickness and death, a general parallel.

1-chronicles-13:10:5.summary: Fire consumes those offering incense, a general case of death for unauthorized approach.

1-chronicles-13:10:6.summary: Nadab and Abihu “died before the Lord” for unauthorized handling, as Oza “died there before God.”
1-chronicles-13:10:6.why: God sanctified among those who draw near.

1-chronicles-13:10:7.summary: Uzziah trespasses on holy duties and is punished (truncated), a broad parallel.

1-chronicles-13:10:8.summary: Joshua going to the priests shares nothing specific with Oza’s death.

1-chronicles-13:11:0.summary: The Lord was angry with Uzzah and struck him; he died there before God, the same event.
1-chronicles-13:11:0.why: Samuel’s account of the same event.

1-chronicles-13:11:1.summary: David feared the Lord that day after the death, Samuel’s parallel to his reaction here.

1-chronicles-13:11:2.summary: Only the phrase “unto this day” is shared; Moses’ burial is unrelated.

1-chronicles-13:11:3.summary: Stones by the ark remain “to this day,” a loose echo of a place named after an ark event.

1-chronicles-13:11:4.summary: God questions Jonah’s grief at His act, loosely like David’s distress at God’s judgment.

1-chronicles-13:11:5.summary: Jonah is “deeply grieved” over God’s action, a general parallel to David’s dismay.

1-chronicles-13:11:6.summary: Only the formula “to this day” is shared; Jacob’s sinew is unrelated.

1-chronicles-13:12:0.summary: The psalmist fears God’s judgments, as David feared God after Oza’s death.

1-chronicles-13:12:1.summary: The Ashkelonites dread receiving the ark after its judgments, like David hesitating to bring it to himself.

1-chronicles-13:12:2.summary: Job’s statement on human lowliness has no specific link to David’s fear about the ark.

1-chronicles-13:12:3.summary: Solomon wonders how God can dwell with people, loosely like David’s question about hosting the ark.

1-chronicles-13:12:4.summary: “To whom shall the ark of the Lord go up away from us?” parallels David’s “How shall I bring God’s ark to myself?”

1-chronicles-13:12:5.summary: Israel fears that whoever touches the Lord’s tent dies, similar dread of holy things.

1-chronicles-13:12:6.summary: Isaiah’s terror before the holy King broadly parallels David’s fear.

1-chronicles-13:12:7.summary: The fearful servant’s complaint about a hard master is unrelated to David’s reverent fear.

1-chronicles-13:12:8.summary: Peter asks the Lord to depart because of his sinfulness, a general parallel to fear of the holy.

1-chronicles-13:13:0.summary: Abdedom appears among the Levite gatekeepers, likely the Abeddara who hosted the ark.
1-chronicles-13:13:0.why: Later role of the ark’s host.

1-chronicles-13:13:1.summary: Abdedom’s sons are listed among the gatekeepers, the family of the ark’s host.

1-chronicles-13:13:3.summary: Abdedom’s many descendants serve in the temple, tied to the man who sheltered the ark.

1-chronicles-13:13:4.summary: The Beerothites fleeing to Gittaim share only a place-like name with “the Geththite.”

1-chronicles-13:13:5.summary: Abdedom serves with instruments before the ark, apparently the same man who hosted it.
1-chronicles-13:13:5.why: Later role of the ark’s host.

1-chronicles-13:14:0.summary: Abdedom had many sons “because God had blessed him,” echoing God blessing Abeddaram.

1-chronicles-13:14:1.summary: The Lord’s blessing makes rich, a general maxim about divine blessing.

1-chronicles-13:14:2.summary: Honoring the Lord brings abundance, a general parallel to God blessing Abeddara’s house.

1-chronicles-13:14:3.summary: Laban is blessed because of Jacob’s presence, loosely like the house blessed by the ark’s presence.

1-chronicles-13:14:4.summary: The Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house and “all that he had” for Joseph’s sake, as God blessed Abeddaram and all that was his.

1-chronicles-13:14:5.summary: God promises to pour out blessing on the house, a general blessing theme.

1-chronicles-14:1:0.summary: Solomon recalls that Chiram sent David cedars to build a house, this same event.

1-chronicles-14:1:4.summary: Chiram king of Tyre supplies cedar and workers for Solomon as he did for David (truncated).

1-chronicles-14:1:2.summary: Cedar from Lebanon via Sidonians and Tyrians for the temple rebuild, a general parallel.

1-chronicles-14:1:3.summary: Hiram supplies cedar timber to Solomon (truncated), the same king who sent David cedar.

1-chronicles-14:1:5.summary: David dwells “in a cedar house,” the palace built with Chiram’s cedar.

1-chronicles-14:1:6.summary: Preparing stone and timber for building is a general parallel.

1-chronicles-14:1:7.summary: A king’s cedar house built unjustly contrasts with David’s house built through Chiram’s gift.

1-chronicles-14:1:8.summary: David says, “I dwell in a cedar house,” the palace from Chiram’s cedar.

1-chronicles-14:1:9.summary: Solomon’s cedar palace (truncated) is a later royal building project.

1-chronicles-14:1:10.summary: Solomon requests Sidonian timber-cutters, a later parallel to Chiram’s workers.

1-chronicles-14:1:11.summary: David appoints quarrymen for God’s house, a general building theme.

1-chronicles-14:1:12.summary: Hiram king of Tyre “had always loved David,” the same friendship shown in the source.

1-chronicles-14:2:0.summary: God anoints David, supports him, and makes him “high among the kings” (truncated), echoing his kingdom increased on high.

1-chronicles-14:2:1.summary: Balaam foresees a ruler whose “kingdom shall increase” and rise high, echoed in David’s kingdom increasing on high.

1-chronicles-14:2:2.summary: Esther’s elevation for the sake of her people loosely parallels David’s exaltation for Israel.

1-chronicles-14:2:3.summary: Chiram says the Lord made Solomon king “because the Lord loves His people,” as David’s kingdom rose “for the sake of His people.”

1-chronicles-14:2:4.summary: God promises David’s house and kingdom will be “made sure for ever,” the establishment David recognizes.

1-chronicles-14:2:5.summary: Because the Lord loves Israel He made the king, matching the kingdom exalted for His people.

1-chronicles-14:2:6.summary: Daniel’s disclaimer about revealed mystery has no link to David’s establishment.

1-chronicles-14:2:7.summary: David acknowledges “Thou didst exalt me, Lord God,” recognizing God raised him.

1-chronicles-14:2:8.summary: Isaiah’s promise to restore Zion’s judges is unrelated to David’s kingdom being established.

1-chronicles-14:2:9.summary: God took David from the sheepfold “to be ruler over My people,” the establishment he now recognizes.
1-chronicles-14:2:9.why: God’s choice of David for Israel.

1-chronicles-14:3:1.summary: David’s sons born in Hebron precede the Jerusalem sons and wives mentioned here.

1-chronicles-14:3:2.summary: The law says the king “shall not multiply wives,” standing against David taking more wives.

1-chronicles-14:3:3.summary: Malachi’s rebuke about abandoning a wife has no direct link to David’s marriages.

1-chronicles-14:3:4.summary: Jesus’ teaching on divorce does not address the source’s report of David’s wives.

1-chronicles-14:3:5.summary: Enjoying life with one’s beloved wife is not specifically linked to David’s added wives.

1-chronicles-14:3:6.summary: The counsel to rejoice in the wife of one’s youth has no specific tie to the source.

1-chronicles-14:3:7.summary: The creation pattern of two becoming one flesh implicitly contrasts with David taking more wives.

1-chronicles-14:3:8.summary: Ecclesiastes’ reflection on ensnaring women is unrelated to David’s family growth.

1-chronicles-14:3:9.summary: Solomon’s many wives turned his heart, a later warning related to royal polygamy.

1-chronicles-14:4:9.summary: The same list of sons born in Jerusalem: Shammua/Samaa, Shobab/Isobaam, Nathan, and Solomon.

1-chronicles-14:4:1.summary: “David begot Solomon” in Jesus’ genealogy names the same Solomon listed here.

1-chronicles-14:4:2.summary: Luke traces Jesus through “Nathan, of David,” the son listed here.

1-chronicles-14:4:3.summary: Nathan the prophet is a different man from David’s son Nathan.

1-chronicles-14:4:4.summary: From David’s many sons, God chose Solomon to sit on the throne.
1-chronicles-14:4:4.why: Significance of Solomon among the sons.

1-chronicles-14:4:5.summary: Solomon’s dream at the start of his reign (truncated) concerns the same son but adds no link to the list.

1-chronicles-14:4:6.summary: David swore that “your son Solomon shall reign after me,” marking the son listed here as heir.

1-chronicles-14:4:7.summary: Solomon’s piety and high-place worship concern the same son, but not the birth list.

1-chronicles-14:4:8.summary: David’s oath that Solomon would reign identifies this son as the heir.

1-chronicles-14:4:10.summary: The promised son “Solomon is his name,” a man of rest who will build God’s house.

1-chronicles-14:4:11.summary: Adonijah concedes the kingdom became his brother’s from the Lord, referring to Solomon indirectly.

1-chronicles-14:4:12.summary: Bathsheba bore a son and named him Solomon, the same son in this list.

1-chronicles-14:5:1.summary: “Ibhar, Elishua” parallel “Ibaar, Elisae” in the list of sons born in Jerusalem.

1-chronicles-14:7:1.summary: “Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet” parallel “Elisamae, Balegdae, and Eliphalet.”

1-chronicles-14:8:0.summary: The Philistines earlier called David “king of the land,” a loose foreshadowing of their reaction here.

1-chronicles-14:8:1.summary: The nations rage when God’s kingdom is established, a typological parallel to the foreigners’ attack.

1-chronicles-14:8:2.summary: The elders “anointed David king over all Israel,” the news that prompts the foreigners’ attack.

1-chronicles-14:8:3.summary: Nations and rulers gather against the Lord’s anointed, as the foreigners go up against anointed David.

1-chronicles-14:8:4.summary: Israel’s elders “anointed David king over Israel,” the event the foreigners hear about.

1-chronicles-14:9:0.summary: The foreigners were “encamped in the Valley of the Giants,” the same place as their attack here.

1-chronicles-14:9:1.summary: “The foreigners came again and again fell upon the Valley of the Giants” repeats this verse.

1-chronicles-14:9:3.summary: The Saints text has “a firm ravine,” not the Valley of the Giants, so the place link is absent.

1-chronicles-14:9:4.summary: The foreigners camped in the Valley of Rephaim, the valley the source calls “Valley of the Giants.”

1-chronicles-14:10:0.summary: Proverbs urges acknowledging wisdom in all ways so the path is made straight, a general parallel to David seeking divine direction before battle.
1-chronicles-14:10:0.why: General principle of seeking guidance before acting.

1-chronicles-14:10:1.summary: The second Philistine attack: David “again inquired of God” and receives tactical instructions, continuing the same inquiry pattern.
1-chronicles-14:10:1.why: Shows David's repeated consultation in the same campaign.

1-chronicles-14:10:3.summary: David inquires “Shall I go up” and the Lord answers “Go up,” the same question-and-answer formula.
1-chronicles-14:10:3.why: Shows David's consistent habit of inquiring before acting.

1-chronicles-14:10:4.summary: David proposes bringing the ark back since it was not sought in Saul's days; contrast of seeking God, but no battle inquiry.
1-chronicles-14:10:4.why: Context of David seeking God unlike Saul.

1-chronicles-14:10:5.summary: God promises to deliver Sisera “into your hand,” a similar divine assurance of victory but different event.
1-chronicles-14:10:5.why: Comparable promise of victory to Israel's leader.

1-chronicles-14:10:6.summary: Ahab's prophets answer “Go up, and the Lord will surely give it into the king's hands,” closely echoing the inquiry formula.
1-chronicles-14:10:6.why: Contrasts genuine inquiry with flattering prophecy.

1-chronicles-14:10:7.summary: “David inquired through the Lord” about pursuing raiders and receives a promise of success, same inquiry pattern.
1-chronicles-14:10:7.why: Another instance of David's inquiry before battle.

1-chronicles-14:10:8.summary: Micaiah echoes “Go up… give it into the king's hand” ironically before revealing defeat; verbal echo with contrasting outcome.
1-chronicles-14:10:8.why: Contrasts true divine answer with false assurance.

1-chronicles-14:10:9.summary: David inquires of the Lord via the ephod about Saul and Keilah and receives a direct answer, same practice of consultation.
1-chronicles-14:10:9.why: Illustrates how David inquired of God.

1-chronicles-14:10:10.summary: David inquires “Shall I go and strike these foreigners?” and the Lord promises to hand them “into your hands.”
1-chronicles-14:10:10.why: Close parallel: inquiry about fighting foreigners and promised victory.

1-chronicles-14:10:11.summary: Samuel's parallel of the second Philistine battle: David inquires and is told not to go up but to circle around.
1-chronicles-14:10:11.why: Parallel account of the same campaign in Samuel.

1-chronicles-14:11:0.summary: Isaiah speaks of the Lord rising as on a mountain and in Gabaon's ravine; the English link to Perazim is not explicit in this Greek wording.
1-chronicles-14:11:0.why: Possible allusion to David's victories near Gibeon.

1-chronicles-14:11:1.summary: Rivers striking a house in a parable share only a water image with David's “cutting of water.”

1-chronicles-14:11:3.summary: Waters overwhelming Pharaoh's army loosely parallels God breaking enemies “like a cutting of water.”
1-chronicles-14:11:3.why: Image of God destroying enemies through water.

1-chronicles-14:11:4.summary: God “gives salvation to kings” and redeems David, general praise for victories like this one.
1-chronicles-14:11:4.why: David credits God for his victories.

1-chronicles-14:11:5.summary: God scatters enemies and lays bare springs of waters at His rebuke, a loosely similar image of divine breakthrough.
1-chronicles-14:11:5.why: Poetic image of God routing enemies.

1-chronicles-14:11:6.summary: David blesses the Lord who trains his hands for war, echoing “by my hand” God's victory.
1-chronicles-14:11:6.why: David attributes battle success to God.

1-chronicles-14:11:7.summary: Job's lament of being struck by God's missiles has no real link to David's victory at Baalpharasin.

1-chronicles-14:11:8.summary: Victory came not by Israel's sword but by God's right hand, paralleling “God has cut through my enemies by my hand.”
1-chronicles-14:11:8.why: Credits God, not human strength, for victory.

1-chronicles-14:12:0.summary: Moses burned the golden calf in fire, a similar act of destroying idols by burning.

1-chronicles-14:12:1.summary: Assyrian kings “put their gods into the fire, for they are not gods,” a close image of burning abandoned gods.
1-chronicles-14:12:1.why: Shows false gods are mere burnable objects.

1-chronicles-14:12:2.summary: The Philistine god Dagon falls before the ark (shown text truncated); Philistine gods humiliated, but no burning.
1-chronicles-14:12:2.why: Philistine gods proven powerless before Israel's God.

1-chronicles-14:12:3.summary: The law commands to “burn the graven images of their gods with fire,” which David's order obeys.
1-chronicles-14:12:3.why: Shows David acted according to the Law.

1-chronicles-14:12:5.summary: God executes vengeance against Egypt's gods, a general theme of judgment on foreign gods.

1-chronicles-14:13:0.summary: The first Philistine raid on “the Valley of the Giants,” which this verse repeats with “again.”
1-chronicles-14:13:0.why: Identifies the first attack being repeated.

1-chronicles-14:13:2.summary: A prophet warns the Syrian king will return next year, a loose parallel of an enemy coming back after defeat.

1-chronicles-14:14:0.summary: The psalmist's desire to dwell in the Lord's house shares only the idea of asking God.
1-chronicles-14:14:0.why: Only a generic link to asking God.

1-chronicles-14:14:1.summary: Jesus's unusual instructions to the blind man have no specific link to David's tactical inquiry.
1-chronicles-14:14:1.why: Only loose idea of following unusual instructions.

1-chronicles-14:14:2.summary: David's first inquiry of God about the foreigners, repeated here when David “again inquired.”
1-chronicles-14:14:2.why: Shows the repeated pattern within the same chapter.

1-chronicles-14:14:3.summary: Joshua is told to set an ambush behind Ai (shown text truncated), a similar divinely directed flanking tactic.

1-chronicles-14:15:0.summary: A sound of many nations as the Lord Sabaoth musters an army; shares a sound signaling divine warfare.
1-chronicles-14:15:0.why: Sound as sign of the Lord's army.

1-chronicles-14:15:1.summary: A sound from heaven like rushing wind signals God's presence, loosely echoing the sound in the treetops.

1-chronicles-14:15:2.summary: God makes the Assyrian king hear a report and retreat; a heard sound used by God in warfare.
1-chronicles-14:15:2.why: God uses heard reports against enemies.

1-chronicles-14:15:3.summary: Paul's call to work out salvation as God works within shares no specific link with the battle signal.
1-chronicles-14:15:3.why: Only an abstract idea of God working.

1-chronicles-14:15:4.summary: The breaker goes up and the Lord leads before them, echoing God going out before His people.
1-chronicles-14:15:4.why: Image of God leading His people into breakthrough.

1-chronicles-14:15:5.summary: God promises Cyrus “I will go before you,” sharing the image of God going before a leader.
1-chronicles-14:15:5.why: God going before His chosen agent.

1-chronicles-14:15:6.summary: Deborah tells Barak “shall not the Lord go before you?” before attacking, matching “God has gone out before you.”
1-chronicles-14:15:6.why: Same assurance that God leads the battle.

1-chronicles-14:15:7.summary: The Lord makes Syria's camp hear the sound of an army, a distinctive divine sound in warfare against an enemy camp.
1-chronicles-14:15:7.why: God using sound to rout enemy camps.

1-chronicles-14:15:8.summary: God tells Gideon to go down to the camp He has delivered into his hand; similar divine signal to attack.
1-chronicles-14:15:8.why: Divine command to attack an enemy camp.

1-chronicles-14:15:9.summary: Jonathan awaits a sign before attacking the foreigners (shown text truncated), a similar signal-based attack.
1-chronicles-14:15:9.why: Sign from God triggering attack on Philistines.

1-chronicles-14:15:10.summary: The sound of a leaf drives the disobedient to flight, a contrasting image of sound in trees causing fear.
1-chronicles-14:15:10.why: Contrast: rustling sound as judgment rather than signal.

1-chronicles-14:15:11.summary: Gideon declares the Lord has given Midian's camp into their hands; a parallel moment of attack upon divine assurance.
1-chronicles-14:15:11.why: Assurance of victory over an enemy camp.

1-chronicles-14:16:0.summary: Jesus calls friends those who “do what I command,” a general theme of obedience.
1-chronicles-14:16:0.why: General theme of obedience to God's command.

1-chronicles-14:16:1.summary: A blessing on doing what one knows shares only a generic obedience idea.

1-chronicles-14:16:2.summary: Noah “did all that the Lord God commanded him,” the same obedience formula as David “did as God commanded him.”

1-chronicles-14:16:3.summary: Mary's “Whatever He tells you, do” shares only a generic obedience idea.

1-chronicles-14:16:5.summary: Mentions Gezer, apparently Gazara, but the Saints spellings differ and the content is unrelated.
1-chronicles-14:16:5.why: Background on the town at the battle's limit.

1-chronicles-14:16:6.summary: “Gazer” among Levitical cities may be the same town as Gazara; place link only.
1-chronicles-14:16:6.why: Locates the endpoint of David's pursuit.

1-chronicles-14:16:7.summary: Israel did “as the Lord commanded Moses,” a similar obedience formula in a different context.

1-chronicles-14:17:0.summary: God puts “the fear of you before all the nations,” fulfilled when the Lord placed David's fear upon all nations.

1-chronicles-14:17:1.summary: Joshua's “name was known throughout the land,” close echo of David having “a name throughout all the land.”

1-chronicles-14:17:2.summary: Nations hear and fear falls on them at the Exodus, a general theme of nations dreading God's people.
1-chronicles-14:17:2.why: Fear of God's people among nations.

1-chronicles-14:17:3.summary: Uzziah's name reaches Egypt, a similar note of a king's widespread fame.

1-chronicles-14:17:4.summary: Foreigners submit to David in his psalm, a general picture of foreign nations' deference.

1-chronicles-14:17:5.summary: The Lord will “lay the dread of you and the fear of you upon all the land,” matching the Lord placing David's fear on nations.

1-chronicles-14:17:6.summary: The Gibeonites feared greatly because of Israel; an example of nations' fear of Israel.

1-chronicles-14:17:7.summary: Rahab says fear of Israel has fallen on Canaan, a parallel theme of God-given dread.
1-chronicles-14:17:7.why: Example of God-given dread among nations.

1-chronicles-15:1:0.summary: The ark is set in “the tent David had pitched for it,” the tent prepared in this verse.

1-chronicles-15:1:1.summary: David vows to “find a place for the Lord,” matching David preparing “the place for God's ark.”
1-chronicles-15:1:1.why: Psalm reflecting David's zeal for the ark's place.

1-chronicles-15:1:2.summary: David contrasts his cedar house with the ark beneath skins, connecting his own houses and the ark's tent.
1-chronicles-15:1:2.why: Develops tension between David's house and God's dwelling.

1-chronicles-15:1:3.summary: David brings the ark “to the place he had prepared for it,” the place mentioned in this verse.
1-chronicles-15:1:3.why: Immediate continuation of the same event.

1-chronicles-15:1:4.summary: Stephen recalls David asking to find a dwelling for the house of Jacob, alluding to David's preparation for God's ark.
1-chronicles-15:1:4.why: New Testament recollection of David's purpose.

1-chronicles-15:1:5.summary: Absalom turning to his own house shares only the word “house.”

1-chronicles-15:1:6.summary: David settles and builds in “the city of David,” where he made houses for himself.
1-chronicles-15:1:6.why: Background for David's building in his city.

1-chronicles-15:1:7.summary: Tamar sent to Amnon's house shares only the word “house.”

1-chronicles-15:2:12.summary: Josiah tells Levites they no longer lift the ark but should minister; related Levitical ark duty.
1-chronicles-15:2:12.why: Later development of Levites' ark role.

1-chronicles-15:2:1.summary: The sons of Levi “bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord,” the rule David invokes.
1-chronicles-15:2:1.why: Legal basis for Levites carrying the ark.

1-chronicles-15:2:2.summary: Levites are joined to Aaron to minister at the Tent (shown text truncated); general Levitical service.

1-chronicles-15:2:3.summary: Priests and Levites carrying the ark of the covenant, the proper bearers David insists on.
1-chronicles-15:2:3.why: Precedent of Levites carrying the ark.

1-chronicles-15:2:5.summary: Kohathites are protected from death by proper handling of holy things; relates to correct bearing of holy objects.
1-chronicles-15:2:5.why: Danger of improper approach to holy things.

1-chronicles-15:2:7.summary: God separates the Levites to be His, supporting “the Lord chose them.”
1-chronicles-15:2:7.why: Shows divine choice of the Levites.

1-chronicles-15:2:8.summary: Rules for Levites' service in the Tent of Testimony; general Levitical ministry.

1-chronicles-15:2:9.summary: The shown text only says Joshua went in to the priests; it does not mention carrying the ark.
1-chronicles-15:2:9.why: Shown text lacks the ark link.

1-chronicles-15:2:10.summary: Kohath's sons “bear them upon their shoulders,” the shoulder-carrying rule behind David's command.
1-chronicles-15:2:10.why: Explains why the ark must be carried by Levites.

1-chronicles-15:2:11.summary: God takes priests and Levites for Himself, a general theme of divine choosing of Levites.

1-chronicles-15:3:1.summary: Solomon assembles all Israel to bring up the ark, a parallel later ark procession.

1-chronicles-15:3:2.summary: David brings the ark up to the city of David with gladness, the parallel Samuel account.

1-chronicles-15:3:3.summary: David “prepared the place for God's ark,” the place referred to in this verse.
1-chronicles-15:3:3.why: Immediate context of the same event.

1-chronicles-15:3:4.summary: The ark is set in the tent David pitched, completion of the event in Samuel's parallel.

1-chronicles-15:3:5.summary: David orders the Levites to bring the ark “to the place I have prepared for it,” repeating this verse's purpose.

1-chronicles-15:4:0.summary: Lists Aaron's sons and their duties, identifying the group David gathered.

1-chronicles-15:4:1.summary: Genealogy of Levi's sons Gedson, Kaath, Merari (shown text truncated), the clans gathered in this chapter.
1-chronicles-15:4:1.why: Background for the Levitical clans listed next.

1-chronicles-15:4:2.summary: Mentions Aaron's sons Eleazar and Ithamar serving as priests; general background on Aaron's line.

1-chronicles-15:4:3.summary: Levites and Aaronites who joined David at Hebron; related groups but different occasion.

1-chronicles-15:4:4.summary: Genealogy of Levi's sons (shown text truncated), background for the Levitical clans.

1-chronicles-15:5:0.summary: Kaath's genealogy includes “Uriel,” likely Ouriel, ruler of Kaath's sons here.

1-chronicles-15:6:0.summary: Merari's genealogy ends with “Asaia his son,” the ruler from Merari's sons here.

1-chronicles-15:7:0.summary: A Gershonite family list naming Joel; possibly the same Joel but not certain.

1-chronicles-15:8:0.summary: Uzziel's son Elzaphan, the ancestor (Elisaphan) of this Levitical group.

1-chronicles-15:9:0.summary: Hebron listed as a son of Kohath, the ancestor of this group.

1-chronicles-15:9:1.summary: “Kaath's sons: … Hebron,” identifying the Hebronite clan.

1-chronicles-15:9:2.summary: Lists Chebron's sons, the same Hebronite family in a later register.
1-chronicles-15:9:2.why: Later list of the Hebronite clan.

1-chronicles-15:9:3.summary: The Chebroni clan's later officials; same clan but different persons.

1-chronicles-15:9:4.summary: Lists the clan of Hebron among Levite clans; general clan reference.

1-chronicles-15:9:5.summary: Kaath's sons include Chebron, the Hebron of this verse.

1-chronicles-15:9:6.summary: Bare list naming Chebron among Kohathite clans.

1-chronicles-15:10:0.summary: Oziel listed among Kaath's four sons, the ancestor of this group.
1-chronicles-15:10:0.why: Identifies Oziel's place in Kohath's line.

1-chronicles-15:10:2.summary: Uzziel's sons Elzaphan and Sithri; names Oziel's line but not Amminadab.

1-chronicles-15:10:3.summary: Uzziel named as a son of Kohath, the Oziel of this verse.

1-chronicles-15:10:4.summary: An Amminadab in Kaath's line; shares the name but genealogy differs from Oziel's line.

1-chronicles-15:11:0.summary: Sadok the mighty young man joining David, same priest summoned here.
1-chronicles-15:11:0.why: Earlier mention of Sadok with David.

1-chronicles-15:11:1.summary: Zadok replaces Abiathar as priest, naming both priests summoned here.
1-chronicles-15:11:1.why: Later fate of the two priests.

1-chronicles-15:11:2.summary: Abiathar escapes to David after Saul's massacre, explaining his attachment to David.

1-chronicles-15:11:3.summary: Sadok listed as priest in David's administration.

1-chronicles-15:11:4.summary: “Zadok and Abiathar were priests,” the same pair under David.

1-chronicles-15:11:5.summary: Zadok, Abiathar and the Levites carry God's ark during Absalom's revolt.
1-chronicles-15:11:5.why: Same priests with the ark later.

1-chronicles-15:11:6.summary: Zadok listed as priest in David's court.

1-chronicles-15:11:7.summary: “Zadok and Abiathar the priests” together with David.

1-chronicles-15:11:8.summary: Abiathar is spared because he carried the ark before David.

1-chronicles-15:12:12.summary: “Rulers of the Levites' ancestral houses,” the exact title David uses here.

1-chronicles-15:12:0.summary: Josiah tells Levites to prepare holy things for brethren; related Levitical consecration.

1-chronicles-15:12:1.summary: Present bodies holy to God; a general theme of consecration for service.

1-chronicles-15:12:2.summary: Moses consecrates the people before God's appearance; similar purification before encountering God.

1-chronicles-15:12:3.summary: “The priests and Levites purified themselves to bring up the ark,” fulfilling this command.

1-chronicles-15:12:4.summary: Priests and Levites “purified themselves” for Hezekiah's Passover; similar wording in different event.

1-chronicles-15:12:5.summary: Priests sanctified at the temple dedication; general consecration for ark ceremony.

1-chronicles-15:12:6.summary: Bringing the ark “to the place he had prepared for it,” same purpose.

1-chronicles-15:12:7.summary: Hezekiah tells Levites “purify yourselves,” a close parallel command.

1-chronicles-15:12:8.summary: “Ancestral rulers of the priests and Levites” with Sadok; related leadership terms in another setting.

1-chronicles-15:12:9.summary: Believers made priests to God shares only a broad priestly theme.

1-chronicles-15:12:10.summary: David “prepared the place for God's ark,” the place named in this command.

1-chronicles-15:12:11.summary: Consecrated Zadokite priests keep the house's duties; general theme of holy priests.

1-chronicles-15:12:13.summary: Jesus prays “Sanctify them,” sharing the general idea of sanctification.

1-chronicles-15:13:0.summary: The ark was carried on a new cart driven by Uzzah, the improper method this verse condemns.

1-chronicles-15:13:1.summary: “Everything done fittingly and in order” echoes doing things “according to judgment.”
1-chronicles-15:13:1.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

1-chronicles-15:13:2.summary: Holding to traditions shares only a vague idea of following prescribed practice.

1-chronicles-15:13:3.summary: Confession of sins has no specific link to the ark's improper transport.
1-chronicles-15:13:3.why: Only general theme of admitting fault.

1-chronicles-15:13:4.summary: Levites “bear the ark,” the rule neglected in the first attempt.

1-chronicles-15:13:6.summary: Kohathites carry holy things “upon their shoulders,” the rule not followed earlier.

1-chronicles-15:13:7.summary: God struck Uzzah and made a “breach,” the event “our God cut among us” recalls.

1-chronicles-15:13:8.summary: Only Levites may lift God's ark, the correction David makes.

1-chronicles-15:13:10.summary: Covering impiety versus explaining reproofs shares only a general confession theme.

1-chronicles-15:13:11.summary: People ate the Passover not “according to the writing” yet were healed; similar failure to follow prescribed order.
1-chronicles-15:13:11.why: Contrast of ritual failure and mercy.
1-chronicles-15:13:11.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

1-chronicles-15:14:0.summary: Levites “purified themselves” by royal command for temple service, close parallel phrasing.

1-chronicles-15:14:1.summary: Consecrate the congregation and priests minister; general consecration theme.

1-chronicles-15:14:2.summary: Levites purified themselves more eagerly than priests; similar purification wording.

1-chronicles-15:14:3.summary: God is sanctified among those who draw near, the principle behind purification.

1-chronicles-15:15:0.summary: Kohathites carry the holy things after covering, the Mosaic instruction followed here.

1-chronicles-15:15:2.summary: The ark's “carrying poles” in Solomon's temple; same poles, different occasion.

1-chronicles-15:15:3.summary: Moses instructs inserting “the carrying poles” to transport the ark, the command referenced.

1-chronicles-15:15:4.summary: Rings for “the carrying poles, so that the ark could be carried,” the design behind proper carrying.

1-chronicles-15:15:5.summary: In this Greek-based wording “consecrated things” replace poles, so the carrying-pole link is not carried.
1-chronicles-15:15:5.why: Greek wording lacks the poles reference.

1-chronicles-15:15:6.summary: Moses placed “the carrying poles” on the ark; same poles but setup rather than carrying.

1-chronicles-15:16:28.summary: Dedication “with songs, harps, lyres, and cymbals,” the same instrument set.

1-chronicles-15:16:0.summary: First ark procession with “psalm singers, lyres, harps… cymbals,” matching instruments.

1-chronicles-15:16:1.summary: Four thousand praise with David's instruments; related organization of musicians.

1-chronicles-15:16:2.summary: “Trumpets and cymbals for sounding out” with instruments for God's songs, same musical role.

1-chronicles-15:16:3.summary: Levites praise with David's songs at the wall dedication; general Levitical music.

1-chronicles-15:16:4.summary: Levites raise their voice with trumpets, cymbals and instruments at the ark's installation.
1-chronicles-15:16:4.why: Parallel musical celebration of the ark.

1-chronicles-15:16:5.summary: Call to exult and shout to God; general joyful praise.

1-chronicles-15:16:6.summary: Praise with psaltery and lyre; shared instruments in praise.

1-chronicles-15:16:7.summary: Tax exemption for singers and Levites (shown text truncated) has no specific link to David's appointment.

1-chronicles-15:16:8.summary: The ark brought up with trumpets, cymbals, harps and lyres, the fulfillment of David's order.

1-chronicles-15:16:9.summary: Judah's unity to carry out the king's ordinance has no specific musical link.

1-chronicles-15:16:10.summary: Qualifications for overseers (shown text truncated) share only the idea of appointing.

1-chronicles-15:16:11.summary: Psalm singers sing and Levites hymn with David's words, continuing David's musical order.

1-chronicles-15:16:12.summary: Appointing elders in churches shares only the word idea “appoint.”

1-chronicles-15:16:13.summary: Titus appointing elders shares only the idea of appointment.

1-chronicles-15:16:14.summary: This Greek-based wording lacks the singers and instruments the English label assumes.
1-chronicles-15:16:14.why: Greek wording drops the music reference.

1-chronicles-15:16:15.summary: Entrusting teaching to faithful people shares only a vague succession idea.

1-chronicles-15:16:16.summary: Gladness heard from far at the wall dedication; shared joyful sound.

1-chronicles-15:16:17.summary: Call to shout and exult to God; general joyful praise.

1-chronicles-15:16:18.summary: Levites with cymbals praise “according to the directions of David,” rooted in this appointment.

1-chronicles-15:16:19.summary: The sound of joy and voices giving thanks in the Lord's house; general joyful sound.
1-chronicles-15:16:19.why: Joyful praise at the Lord's house.

1-chronicles-15:16:21.summary: David appoints Asaph, Aiman and Idithon's sons with instruments and cymbals (shown text truncated).

1-chronicles-15:16:22.summary: In David's days Asaph led the singers, recalling David's appointment of singers.

1-chronicles-15:16:23.summary: Kings as foster fathers has no link to appointing musicians.

1-chronicles-15:16:24.summary: A thanksgiving psalm calling to shout to the Lord; general joyful praise.

1-chronicles-15:16:25.summary: David addresses the same “rulers of the Levites,” immediately prior in the same scene.

1-chronicles-15:16:26.summary: Making music with psaltery and lyre to God; shared instruments of praise.

1-chronicles-15:16:27.summary: Praise with tambourine and psaltery; general musical praise.

1-chronicles-15:17:0.summary: “Heman the psalm singer, son of Joel,” the same Aiman son of Joel.

1-chronicles-15:17:1.summary: “Ethan son of Kisai” of Merari, the same Aithan son of Kisaiou.

1-chronicles-15:17:3.summary: The shown Greek-numbered verse lacks the superscription; link to Asaph only through the psalm's attribution.

1-chronicles-15:17:4.summary: Asaph, Aiman and Idithon appointed as musicians with their sons (shown text truncated).

1-chronicles-15:17:5.summary: Samuel's firstborn Joel, father of Heman per 1 Chr 6, but link needs that genealogy.

1-chronicles-15:18:0.summary: Abdedom's sons listed among gatekeepers, the same Abdedom.

1-chronicles-15:18:2.summary: The ark stayed in Abeddara's house; likely the same Abdedom (Obed-edom).

1-chronicles-15:18:3.summary: Abdedom's lot as gatekeeper, the same gatekeeper.

1-chronicles-15:18:4.summary: Lists Zacharias, Jiiel, Semiramoth, Eliab, Banaias, Abdedom with instruments, many of the same names.

1-chronicles-15:18:5.summary: Abdedom's sons as laborers, the same gatekeeper family.

1-chronicles-15:18:6.summary: Lists of musicians' sons (shown text truncated); related singers but different names.

1-chronicles-15:18:7.summary: Abdedom and his brethren as gatekeepers, same person and role.

1-chronicles-15:19:2.summary: “Asaph sounded the cymbals,” matching his cymbal role here.

1-chronicles-15:19:3.summary: “Trumpets and cymbals for sounding out,” the same musical function.

1-chronicles-15:19:4.summary: David orders singers with cymbals “to sound on high,” the order carried out here.

1-chronicles-15:19:5.summary: Earlier procession with psalm singers and cymbals; similar instruments.
