1-chronicles-21:16:0.summary: Moses and Aaron “fell on their faces,” a shared gesture of crisis prostration.

1-chronicles-21:16:1.summary: Ahab puts on sackcloth in repentance, generally like David and the elders in sackcloth.

1-chronicles-21:16:2.summary: Joshua lifts his eyes, sees a figure “with a drawn sword in his hand,” and falls on his face, closely parallel.

1-chronicles-21:16:3.summary: Nineveh’s king and people in sackcloth repent before God, a general parallel to sackcloth repentance.

1-chronicles-21:16:4.summary: The psalmist wears sackcloth and humbles himself, a general mourning parallel.

1-chronicles-21:16:5.summary: Elisha’s servant sees a heavenly army when his eyes are opened, a loose parallel to seeing the angel.

1-chronicles-21:16:6.summary: The angel of God stands between Egypt and Israel, loosely like the angel standing between earth and heaven.

1-chronicles-21:16:7.summary: Cherubim with a flaming sword guard Eden, a general image of an angelic sword.

1-chronicles-21:16:8.summary: Moses and Aaron fall on their faces pleading that one man’s sin not bring wrath on all, as David pleads.

1-chronicles-21:16:9.summary: Balaam sees “the Lord’s angel” with “his sword drawn in his hand” and falls on his face, a close parallel.

1-chronicles-21:16:10.summary: Hezekiah puts on sackcloth in crisis, a general parallel to David’s sackcloth.

1-chronicles-21:16:11.summary: Wisdom’s word leaping from heaven as a warrior with “a sharp sword” into a doomed land echoes the destroying angel.

1-chronicles-21:16:12.summary: The destroyer “touched heaven while standing upon the earth,” echoing the angel “standing between earth and heaven.”

1-chronicles-21:17:0.summary: Ezekiel’s shame upon God’s propitiation shares nothing specific with David’s confession.

1-chronicles-21:17:1.summary: David’s penitential plea for rescue from bloodguilt generally parallels his confession here.

1-chronicles-21:17:2.summary: God visits fathers’ sins on descendants, loosely related to David’s plea that punishment fall on his house.

1-chronicles-21:17:3.summary: Moses offers himself to be blotted out for the people’s sin, paralleling David’s plea to bear the punishment.

1-chronicles-21:17:4.summary: “I sinned and did evil before Thee” closely echoes David’s “I am the one who sinned; in doing evil I did evil.”

1-chronicles-21:17:5.summary: Judah offers himself in Benjamin’s place, a general substitution parallel.

1-chronicles-21:17:6.summary: Hezekiah accepts judgment on his descendants for peace in his days, the reverse of David’s plea; only a loose contrast.

1-chronicles-21:17:7.summary: Israel given “like sheep” to slaughter loosely echoes David calling the people “sheep.”

1-chronicles-21:17:8.summary: One party’s turning away brings wrath on “all Israel,” a general parallel to collective punishment.

1-chronicles-21:17:9.summary: The good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep, a typological echo of David shielding his “sheep.”

1-chronicles-21:17:11.summary: Laying down one’s life for others generally parallels David’s willingness to bear punishment.

1-chronicles-21:17:12.summary: David taken from the sheepfold to rule Israel underlies his calling the people “sheep.”

1-chronicles-21:17:13.summary: Samuel’s parallel opens the census story: the Lord incited David to “count Israel and Judah.”

1-chronicles-21:17:14.summary: David earlier says “I have sinned greatly in doing this thing,” the same census confession.

1-chronicles-21:17:15.summary: Paul wishes himself accursed for his kinsmen, a general parallel to David’s self-offering.

1-chronicles-21:17:16.summary: God’s wrath against “the sheep of Thy pasture” loosely echoes David’s plea for the sheep.

1-chronicles-21:17:17.summary: The sword on David’s house loosely relates to David asking that God’s hand fall on his house.

1-chronicles-21:17:18.summary: Israel as a flock without a shepherd generally relates to the people as “sheep.”

1-chronicles-21:18:0.summary: The temple was built at “the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite,” the site David is told to use.

1-chronicles-21:18:3.summary: The angel stood “at the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite,” the same place named here.

1-chronicles-21:18:2.summary: Gad brings the Lord’s message to David earlier in the same episode.
1-chronicles-21:18:2.why: Gad as messenger in the story.

1-chronicles-21:18:4.summary: An angel directing Philip shares only the motif of an angel giving instructions (shown text truncated).

1-chronicles-21:19:0.summary: “Whatever He tells you, do” shares only a general obedience theme with David’s compliance.

1-chronicles-21:19:1.summary: Naaman is urged to obey the prophet’s word, a general parallel to obeying a prophet’s instruction (truncated).

1-chronicles-21:19:2.summary: Saul told to enter the city for instructions has no specific link to David going up.

1-chronicles-21:20:0.summary: Gideon “beating out wheat” when the Lord’s messenger appears parallels Orna “threshing wheat” when the angel is seen.

1-chronicles-21:21:1.summary: Abigail bows before David with her face to the ground, a similar gesture of homage to David.

1-chronicles-21:22:0.summary: Ahab says “Give me your vineyard … I will give you silver,” a close parallel royal land request, contrasting in outcome.

1-chronicles-21:22:2.summary: “The plague against the sons of Israel stopped” after Phinehas acted, parallel to the plague ceasing.

1-chronicles-21:22:3.summary: Aaron stood between the dead and the living “and the outbreak subsided,” paralleling the plague ceasing.

1-chronicles-21:23:1.summary: The cart’s wood is split and cows offered as a “whole burnt offering,” paralleling Orna’s offer of oxen and wagons for wood.

1-chronicles-21:23:2.summary: The Hittites offer Abraham burial land freely, paralleling Orna offering his land to David.

1-chronicles-21:23:3.summary: Jeremiah is offered a field to acquire, a general land-transaction parallel.

1-chronicles-21:23:4.summary: Elisha sacrifices his oxen and boils them with the oxen’s equipment, like Orna offering calves and plow for wood.

1-chronicles-21:23:5.summary: Isaiah’s threshing parable shares only agricultural wagon imagery.

1-chronicles-21:24:0.summary: Not appearing before the Lord “empty” generally relates to David refusing a costless offering.

1-chronicles-21:24:1.summary: Abraham insists, “Take the silver of the field from me,” as David insists on paying full price.
1-chronicles-21:24:1.why: Insisting on paying for sacred land.

1-chronicles-21:24:2.summary: Abram refuses to take “anything that is yours,” echoing David’s “I will not take what is yours.”

1-chronicles-21:24:3.summary: Malachi condemns offering seized or damaged animals, contrasting with David’s costly offering.

1-chronicles-21:24:4.summary: Paul’s instruction about honorable conduct has no specific link to David’s purchase.

1-chronicles-21:26:6.summary: “Fire came down from heaven and consumed the whole burnt offerings” at Solomon’s temple, the same site and sign.
1-chronicles-21:26:6.why: Same divine fire at the same place.

1-chronicles-21:26:14.summary: Samuel offers a whole burnt offering, “cried to the Lord,” and was heard, paralleling David’s cry and answer.

1-chronicles-21:26:0.summary: “Fire came out from the Lord and consumed” the whole burnt offerings, the same sign of acceptance.

1-chronicles-21:26:1.summary: Fire from the rock consumes Gideon’s offering, a parallel sign of divine acceptance.

1-chronicles-21:26:2.summary: Prayers of the upright are acceptable to God, a general theme of accepted worship.

1-chronicles-21:26:3.summary: “Fire from the Lord fell from heaven and consumed the burnt offering” at Carmel closely parallels David’s answer.

1-chronicles-21:26:4.summary: Moses builds an altar and offers whole burnt offerings and deliverance sacrifices, a general cultic parallel.

1-chronicles-21:26:5.summary: A prayer to open the lips in praise has no specific link to David’s altar and fire.

1-chronicles-21:26:7.summary: “The God who answers by fire—He is God” matches the Lord answering David “with fire from heaven.”

1-chronicles-21:26:8.summary: Instructions for altars with whole burnt offerings and deliverance sacrifices provide general background.

1-chronicles-21:26:9.summary: “Cry out to Me and I will answer you” generally parallels David crying and being answered.

1-chronicles-21:26:10.summary: The temple was built at Orna’s threshing floor, “the place David had prepared,” where this altar stood.

1-chronicles-21:26:11.summary: The flame rising from Manoah’s altar with the Lord’s messenger loosely parallels heavenly fire at an altar.

1-chronicles-21:26:12.summary: A call to worship at God’s holy mountain shares only a general worship theme.

1-chronicles-21:26:13.summary: “He will call upon Me, and I will hear him” generally parallels God answering David’s cry.

1-chronicles-21:26:15.summary: God answering before they cry generally parallels the Lord answering David.

1-chronicles-21:26:16.summary: 2 Maccabees recalls “fire came down from heaven and consumed” offerings, the same tradition of heavenly fire.
1-chronicles-21:26:16.why: Tradition of heavenly fire on altar.

1-chronicles-21:27:0.summary: Angels as ministering spirits sent out generally relate to the angel obeying the Lord’s command.

1-chronicles-21:27:1.summary: Jesus says “Put the sword into the sheath,” a close verbal echo of the angel sheathing his sword.

1-chronicles-21:27:2.summary: The Saints text of Ezekiel 21:35 lacks the sheath wording the label assumes, so no link remains.

1-chronicles-21:27:3.summary: The “sword of the Lord” is told, “Return to your sheath,” closely matching the angel sheathing the sword.

1-chronicles-21:27:4.summary: Jesus says “Return your sword to its place,” a verbal echo in an unrelated context.

1-chronicles-21:27:5.summary: Angels “doing His word” generally fits the angel obeying the Lord’s command.

1-chronicles-21:27:7.summary: Gad’s options name the “Lord’s sword” and “Lord’s angel destroying,” the sword now sheathed.

1-chronicles-21:27:8.summary: Orna seeing the king while threshing has no direct link to the angel sheathing the sword.
1-chronicles-21:27:8.why: Same chapter but no direct link.

1-chronicles-21:27:9.summary: Samuel’s parallel tells the Lord commanding the angel, “Now withdraw your hand,” the same event.

1-chronicles-21:29:2.summary: Solomon came “from the bama in Gabaon … from before the Tent of Testimony,” the same tent location.

1-chronicles-21:29:1.summary: The Tent “which Moses … had made in the wilderness” was at the high place in Gabaon, matching this verse.

1-chronicles-21:29:3.summary: Moses erects the Tent and the altar of offerings, the origin of the tent mentioned (shown text truncated).

1-chronicles-21:29:4.summary: Solomon offers a thousand burnt offerings on the altar at Gibeon, the same altar location (truncated).

1-chronicles-21:30:0.summary: A heavenly hymn about fearing God shares only a general fear theme.

1-chronicles-21:30:1.summary: Serving God with reverence because He is a consuming fire loosely relates to David’s fear.

1-chronicles-21:30:2.summary: John falls as dead before the heavenly Christ, a general reaction of terror to a heavenly vision.

1-chronicles-21:30:3.summary: God’s call to fear Him who bounds the sea has no specific link to David’s fear of the angel.

1-chronicles-21:30:4.summary: “I feared Thy judgments” generally parallels David’s fear of the angel’s judgment.

1-chronicles-21:30:5.summary: Job’s agitation about God is only a general fear theme.

1-chronicles-21:30:6.summary: “David feared God that day,” a parallel instance of David’s fear inhibiting approach to God’s holy things.

1-chronicles-21:30:8.summary: Job’s agitation at remembering suffering has no specific link.

1-chronicles-21:30:9.summary: “David feared the Lord that day” after judgment at the ark, a similar fear after divine striking.

1-chronicles-21:30:11.summary: Job asks God to keep His terrifying hand away, a general fear-of-God parallel.

1-chronicles-21:30:12.summary: Deuteronomy’s command to fear and love God is generic and does not specifically link.

1-chronicles-21:30:13.summary: “Who knows the might of Thine anger” generally relates to fear of God’s wrath.

1-chronicles-21:3:10.summary: 1 Kings 14:16 has no corresponding passage in this edition, which follows the Greek text; there is no Saints reading to compare.
1-chronicles-21:3:10.why: Compare a Hebrew-based translation if this passage matters for study.
1-chronicles-21:3:10.note: Passage unavailable in this edition; the review records the absence rather than an interpretation.

1-chronicles-21:30:7.summary: Jeremiah 10:7 has no corresponding passage in this edition, which follows the Greek text; there is no Saints reading to compare.
1-chronicles-21:30:7.why: Compare a Hebrew-based translation if this passage matters for study.
1-chronicles-21:30:7.note: Passage unavailable in this edition; the review records the absence rather than an interpretation.

1-chronicles-22:1:0.summary: The Lord’s house was built at Orna’s threshing floor, the site David designates as the house of God.

1-chronicles-22:1:2.summary: Jacob says “This is none other than the house of God,” closely echoing David’s “This is the house of the Lord God.”

1-chronicles-22:1:3.summary: God chose Jerusalem for His name, generally supporting the choice of this site.

1-chronicles-22:1:4.summary: Gad commands an altar on Orna’s threshing floor, the parallel origin of this altar.

1-chronicles-22:1:5.summary: Worship centralized at “this altar” in Jerusalem relates loosely to David designating the altar.

1-chronicles-22:1:6.summary: Deuteronomy’s “place which the Lord your God shall choose” for whole burnt offerings is fulfilled in this site.

1-chronicles-22:1:7.summary: Debate over Jerusalem as the place of worship loosely relates to this founding designation.

1-chronicles-22:1:8.summary: God rejected Shiloh’s tent, a loose contrast with choosing the new site.

1-chronicles-22:1:9.summary: “The Lord chose Zion … here I will dwell,” matching David’s identification of God’s house.

1-chronicles-22:1:10.summary: God chose Mount Zion and “built His sanctuary” there, the outcome of David’s designation.

1-chronicles-22:1:11.summary: The chosen place for whole burnt offerings in Deuteronomy is realized in this altar.

1-chronicles-22:1:12.summary: Hezekiah’s centralizing at “this altar” in Jerusalem loosely relates to this altar’s designation.

1-chronicles-22:2:0.summary: Solomon subjects the remaining non-Israelite peoples to labor, parallel to David conscripting resident foreigners.

1-chronicles-22:2:1.summary: Solomon gathers “all the resident foreign men in Israel’s land” after David’s numbering, the same workforce.

1-chronicles-22:2:3.summary: Money for builders and “quarried stones” for the house loosely parallels preparing dressed stones.

1-chronicles-22:2:4.summary: Remaining non-Israelites brought under tribute by Solomon parallel David’s use of resident foreigners.

1-chronicles-22:2:5.summary: Gentiles alienated from Israel share only the “stranger” idea, not the building labor.

1-chronicles-22:2:6.summary: Former “resident foreigners” built into a holy sanctuary loosely echoes foreigners preparing stones for God’s house.

1-chronicles-22:2:7.summary: Chiram sends wall builders and carpenters to build David’s house, a general building parallel.

1-chronicles-22:2:8.summary: Silver for stonecutters to build the second temple loosely parallels preparing stonecutters.

1-chronicles-22:2:9.summary: Foreigners serving as laborers for Israel is a general parallel to the conscripted foreigners.

1-chronicles-22:2:10.summary: Hiram sends stoneworkers to build David a house, a general building parallel.

1-chronicles-22:2:11.summary: Costly cut stones used in Solomon’s buildings show the dressed stones David prepared.

1-chronicles-22:2:12.summary: “Stone quarriers” and quarried stones for the Lord’s house parallel David’s quarrymen.

1-chronicles-22:2:13.summary: The house was built of stones cut beforehand, showing the use of the stones David had prepared.

1-chronicles-22:3:0.summary: David again lists “bronze and iron beyond weighing,” repeating this verse’s abundance formula.

1-chronicles-22:3:1.summary: There was “no measured weight of the bronze … because of its great abundance,” echoing bronze “beyond weighing.”

1-chronicles-22:3:3.summary: Leaders give bronze and iron for the house, adding to David’s preparation of these metals.

1-chronicles-22:3:4.summary: The temple bronze “was beyond weighing,” the same phrase used of David’s bronze.

1-chronicles-22:3:5.summary: Solomon’s vessels used bronze in such abundance that the weight “did not run out,” matching bronze beyond weighing.

1-chronicles-22:4:1.summary: Sidonians (“Sedanin”) and Tyrians (“Sorin”) bring cedar timber for the second temple, echoing their cedar supply to David.

1-chronicles-22:4:2.summary: Hiram king of Tyre sent David “cedar wood,” the same Tyrian cedar supply.

1-chronicles-22:4:3.summary: Solomon recalls that Chiram of Tyre “sent him cedars,” confirming the Tyrian cedar supply to David.

1-chronicles-22:5:0.summary: Solomon calls himself “a little child,” matching David’s description of him as “a tender child.”

1-chronicles-22:5:2.summary: Jesus knowing His hour had come shares only a vague before-death setting.

1-chronicles-22:5:3.summary: John the Baptist’s “He must increase” has no specific link to David preparing for Solomon.

1-chronicles-22:5:4.summary: The temple “adorned with beautiful stones” loosely relates to the house built to greatness.

1-chronicles-22:5:5.summary: One labors and another reaps, loosely like David preparing and Solomon building.

1-chronicles-22:5:6.summary: Elders weep remembering the first house, loosely recalling the glory of the temple David envisioned.

1-chronicles-22:5:7.summary: Haggai recalls “this house in its former glory,” the glorious temple David planned.

1-chronicles-22:5:8.summary: Peter prepares others before his departure, a loose parallel to David preparing before his death.

1-chronicles-22:5:9.summary: Ezekiel’s misused ornaments have no specific link to David’s temple preparations.

1-chronicles-22:5:10.summary: The “lofty house” becoming an object of astonishment at its ruin contrasts with its intended renown.

1-chronicles-22:5:11.summary: Haggai promises greater glory for “this house,” loosely recalling the temple’s intended glory.

1-chronicles-22:5:12.summary: The glorious house burned with fire contrasts with the glory David intended for it.

1-chronicles-22:5:13.summary: Rehoboam is “younger and cowardly in heart,” a loose verbal echo of a “tender” young heir.

1-chronicles-22:5:14.summary: Moses, unable to enter the land, prepares Joshua to succeed him, as David prepares for Solomon (truncated).

1-chronicles-22:5:15.summary: Solomon says “The house I am building is great,” fulfilling David’s wish that it rise to greatness.

1-chronicles-22:5:16.summary: Jesus’ saying about working while it is day has no specific link.

1-chronicles-22:5:17.summary: The “lofty house” becoming an object of hissing contrasts with its intended renown.

1-chronicles-22:5:18.summary: Ecclesiastes’ counsel to work before Hades is only a generic theme.

1-chronicles-22:6:0.summary: Moses commissions Joshua as successor, paralleling David charging Solomon.

1-chronicles-22:6:1.summary: Paul’s farewell charge to the elders is a general parallel to a departing leader’s charge (truncated).

1-chronicles-22:6:2.summary: Paul’s charge to Timothy about impartiality shares only the act of charging.

1-chronicles-22:6:3.summary: Jesus’ instructions to the apostles before ascension have no specific link.

1-chronicles-22:6:4.summary: Paul solemnly commands Timothy to keep the commandment, a general charge parallel (truncated).

1-chronicles-22:6:5.summary: Moses commands Joshua, “Be courageous and strong,” the model for David’s charge to Solomon.

1-chronicles-22:6:6.summary: The Great Commission shares only the act of commanding.

1-chronicles-22:6:7.summary: Moses is told to instruct Joshua before the congregation, paralleling David’s charge to his successor.

1-chronicles-22:6:8.summary: Paul’s solemn charge to Timothy shares only the act of charging.

1-chronicles-22:6:9.summary: Near death Moses is told to call Joshua to be commanded, paralleling David calling Solomon.

1-chronicles-22:7:0.summary: David vows to find “a dwelling for the God of Jacob,” the same desire to build God a house.

1-chronicles-22:7:1.summary: The place God chooses “to set His name there” is background for a house for the Lord’s name.

1-chronicles-22:7:3.summary: “It came upon the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the Lord” closely matches David’s words.

1-chronicles-22:7:4.summary: The place chosen “for His name to be called upon” is general background to a house for the name.

1-chronicles-22:7:5.summary: David tells Nathan of the ark in a tent, the original occasion of his wish to build.

1-chronicles-22:7:6.summary: David tells the assembly, “It came upon my heart to build a house,” repeating this same speech (truncated).

1-chronicles-22:7:7.summary: A law about slaughtering far from the chosen place has no specific link to David’s wish.

1-chronicles-22:7:8.summary: Solomon is “building a house for the name of the Lord my God,” fulfilling David’s intention.

1-chronicles-22:7:9.summary: God consecrates the built house “to put My name there,” the fulfilment of the plan.

1-chronicles-22:7:10.summary: David says he delights in “my God’s house,” giving more for it, the same devotion to building.

1-chronicles-22:7:11.summary: Solomon prays toward the place where God said “My name shall be there,” general fulfilment.

1-chronicles-22:7:12.summary: Darius’ decree protecting the house shares only the “name dwells there” phrasing.

1-chronicles-22:7:13.summary: David tells Nathan the ark is beneath skins and God answers about the house, the episode recalled here (truncated).

1-chronicles-22:8:2.summary: God says “You shall not build Me a house,” the word David recalls here (truncated; blood reason not shown).

1-chronicles-22:8:3.summary: Samuel’s parallel: “You will not build Me a house for Me to dwell in,” the same divine word (truncated).

1-chronicles-22:8:4.summary: Purification of clothes after battle shares only the idea of bloodshed defilement, not mentioned in the text shown.

1-chronicles-22:8:5.summary: Purifying articles after war has no specific link to David’s bloodshed barring him from building.

1-chronicles-22:9:0.summary: “He had peace on every side” and Israel lived securely all Solomon’s days, fulfilling the promise of rest and peace.

1-chronicles-22:9:2.summary: Israel eating, drinking and rejoicing under Solomon loosely reflects promised peace.

1-chronicles-22:9:3.summary: The birth and naming of Solomon, loved by the Lord, is the son promised here.

1-chronicles-22:9:4.summary: A child born whose peace has no limit on David’s throne echoes the promised son of peace.

1-chronicles-22:9:5.summary: “Abundant peace” in the king’s days, in a psalm for Solomon, echoes peace in his days.

1-chronicles-22:9:6.summary: Isaiah’s river of peace for Jerusalem shares only the word “peace.”

1-chronicles-22:9:7.summary: God making peace and calamity is a general statement with no specific link.

1-chronicles-22:9:8.summary: Gideon’s altar named Peace of the Lord shares only the word “peace.”

1-chronicles-22:9:9.summary: Job’s statement that God provides quiet is too general to link.

1-chronicles-22:9:10.summary: God chose Solomon to build His house and be His son, repeating this promise.

1-chronicles-22:9:11.summary: A prayer for peace shares only the word “peace.”

1-chronicles-22:9:12.summary: “Peace upon peace” to far and near shares only the word.

1-chronicles-22:9:13.summary: God promises peace in the temple place, loosely tying peace to the house.

1-chronicles-22:9:14.summary: God promises to raise David’s offspring from his body, the dynastic promise behind this verse.

1-chronicles-22:9:15.summary: Samuel’s parallel: David’s seed “will build Me a house for My name,” the same promise.

1-chronicles-22:9:16.summary: Sirach recalls Solomon reigned in peace, with God giving “rest all around” to build His house.

1-chronicles-22:10:2.summary: Samuel’s parallel: he will build a house, “I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to Me.”

1-chronicles-22:10:0.summary: Hebrews quotes “I will be a Father to Him, and He will be a Son to Me,” applying it to Christ.

1-chronicles-22:10:3.summary: Rule “upon the throne of David and his kingdom … for ever” echoes the eternal throne promise.

1-chronicles-22:10:4.summary: The man called Rising “will build the Lord’s house” and rule on his throne, echoing the builder-king promise.

1-chronicles-22:10:5.summary: The king calls God “my Father,” echoing the Father-son relationship promised.

1-chronicles-22:10:6.summary: Solomon cites God’s word that David’s son “shall build the house for My name,” this promise.

1-chronicles-22:10:8.summary: David’s seed and throne established “for ever,” matching the eternal throne promise.

1-chronicles-22:10:9.summary: “Your son … shall build the house for My name,” and Solomon declares it fulfilled.

1-chronicles-22:11:0.summary: David says again “the Lord be with you,” repeating this blessing in the same speech.

1-chronicles-22:11:1.summary: A prayer for peace has no specific link to the Lord being with Solomon.

1-chronicles-22:11:3.summary: “I am with you all the days” echoes the assurance “the Lord will be with you.”

1-chronicles-22:11:4.summary: Emmanuel, “God with us,” shares only the general with-you idea.

1-chronicles-22:11:5.summary: A closing blessing “God of peace be with you” is a generic formula.

1-chronicles-22:11:6.summary: “The Lord be with your spirit” is a generic closing blessing.

1-chronicles-22:12:0.summary: God gives wisdom to those who ask, generally matching David’s wish for Solomon’s wisdom.

1-chronicles-22:12:1.summary: Solomon asks, “give me wisdom and understanding,” the very gift David prays for him.

1-chronicles-22:12:2.summary: A proverb about the wisdom of resourceful people has no specific link.

1-chronicles-22:12:4.summary: Keeping commandments as knowing God shares only a generic obedience theme.

1-chronicles-22:12:5.summary: Keeping and doing the law “is your wisdom and understanding,” linking wisdom and law as David does.

1-chronicles-22:12:6.summary: A prayer “For Solomon” asking God to give judgment to the king’s son parallels David’s prayer.

1-chronicles-22:12:7.summary: Jesus promising wisdom to disciples on trial has no specific link.

1-chronicles-22:12:8.summary: “The Lord gives wisdom … understanding” generally echoes David’s prayer.

1-chronicles-22:12:9.summary: Solomon’s later heart turned from the Lord contrasts with David’s charge to keep the law (truncated).

1-chronicles-22:13:2.summary: The kingdom is established “if he remains strong to observe My commandments and My judgments,” the same condition.

1-chronicles-22:13:3.summary: Paul’s call to be strengthened in the Lord is a generic encouragement.

1-chronicles-22:13:4.summary: David charges Solomon to keep judgments “written in Moses’ law,” a parallel charge.

1-chronicles-22:13:5.summary: “Be courageous and strong; fear not … neither be terrified,” the same formula Moses gave Joshua.

1-chronicles-22:13:6.summary: Fulfilling the royal law of love has no specific link.

1-chronicles-22:13:7.summary: Paul tells his child to be strengthened in grace, only a generic echo.

1-chronicles-22:13:8.summary: David tells Solomon, chosen to build, “Be strong and act,” the same charge.

1-chronicles-22:13:9.summary: Not being ashamed when regarding commandments is a generic link.

1-chronicles-22:13:10.summary: “Only be strong and courageous!” repeats the commissioning formula.

1-chronicles-22:13:11.summary: Trusting the Lord to “prosper” loosely parallels the promise of success.

1-chronicles-22:13:12.summary: God’s witness that David will do His will has no specific link to this charge.

1-chronicles-22:13:13.summary: Bearing burdens to fulfil Christ’s law shares only the word “law.”

1-chronicles-22:13:14.summary: “Be courageous; be strong” verbally echoes David’s charge, though in another setting.

1-chronicles-22:13:15.summary: Jesus fulfilling righteousness at baptism has no specific link.

1-chronicles-22:13:16.summary: Kings on David’s throne prosper if they carry out God’s word, generally like conditional success.

1-chronicles-22:14:0.summary: David prepared iron and bronze “beyond weighing,” the same preparations restated.

1-chronicles-22:14:2.summary: Solomon’s yearly gold income loosely relates to vast gold quantities.

1-chronicles-22:14:3.summary: The temple bronze “had no reckoned weight,” echoing bronze beyond weighing.

1-chronicles-22:14:4.summary: Temple bronze “was beyond weighing,” the same phrase.

1-chronicles-22:14:5.summary: Generosity from “deep poverty” loosely echoes David giving “according to my poverty.”

1-chronicles-22:15:0.summary: Weaving the ephod’s shoulder-piece shares only skilled craftsmanship.

1-chronicles-22:15:1.summary: Bezalel is skilled “in every kind of work,” including stone and wood, paralleling the skilled workers.

1-chronicles-22:15:2.summary: Designing in every craft for the tabernacle generally parallels the skilled workers.

1-chronicles-22:15:3.summary: Craftsmen filled with skill “to do all the work of the sanctuary” generally parallel the workers.
1-chronicles-22:15:3.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

1-chronicles-22:15:4.summary: Hiram, skilled “for doing every work in bronze,” is an actual craftsman of Solomon’s temple.

1-chronicles-22:16:0.summary: “The Lord will be with you,” the same blessing earlier in David’s speech.

1-chronicles-22:16:1.summary: “Arise from the dead” shares only the word “arise.”

1-chronicles-22:16:2.summary: Strength in Christ for all things is a generic theme.

1-chronicles-22:16:3.summary: Abounding in “the Lord’s work” loosely parallels the call to act in God’s building work.

1-chronicles-22:16:4.summary: “Be strong … for the Lord your God is with you” matches the charge “Arise and act, and the Lord be with you.”

1-chronicles-22:16:5.summary: Working out salvation shares no specific element.

1-chronicles-22:16:6.summary: “Arise!” to Joshua after defeat shares only the word.

1-chronicles-22:16:7.summary: “As I was with Moses, so I will be with you” echoes the Lord-with-you assurance to a successor.

1-chronicles-22:16:8.summary: Deborah’s “Arise!” with the Lord going before Barak loosely echoes the call to act.

1-chronicles-22:16:9.summary: “Arise and cross” to Joshua after Moses’ death loosely parallels a successor told to arise.

1-chronicles-22:16:11.summary: The Danites’ “Arise” to attack Laish shares only the word.

1-chronicles-22:16:12.summary: “The Lord will be with you as He was with my father” echoes the blessing formula.

1-chronicles-22:16:13.summary: Iron and bronze prepared “beyond weighing,” matching metals beyond counting.

1-chronicles-22:16:14.summary: Saul’s “Go, and the Lord will be with you” echoes the blessing to act.

1-chronicles-22:16:15.summary: “The Lord will be with you” in Jehoshaphat’s day echoes the blessing formula.

1-chronicles-22:17:0.summary: David assembles all Israel’s rulers to present Solomon as builder, the same appeal (truncated).

1-chronicles-22:17:1.summary: Paul asking help for co-workers shares only a generic help theme.

1-chronicles-22:17:2.summary: Supporting missionaries shares only the word “support.”

1-chronicles-22:17:3.summary: Israel’s rulers and commanders offer eagerly for the house, fulfilling David’s command.

1-chronicles-22:17:4.summary: Paul’s commendation of Phoebe has no specific link.

1-chronicles-22:18:0.summary: God promised “rest from all the enemies round about,” fulfilled in rest on every side.

1-chronicles-22:18:1.summary: David says the Lord “has given rest to His people,” the same statement.

1-chronicles-22:18:2.summary: The Lord gave David possession “on every side, away from all his surrounding enemies,” same rest.

1-chronicles-22:18:3.summary: God’s hand subdued nations to give the land, generally like inhabitants given into hand.

1-chronicles-22:18:4.summary: “If God is for us” is too general a parallel.

1-chronicles-22:18:5.summary: God delivers the foreigners into David’s hands, one instance of the subjugation mentioned.

1-chronicles-22:18:6.summary: The Church having peace shares only a generic peace theme.

1-chronicles-22:18:7.summary: Rest “from all your enemies round about,” then worship at the chosen place, matches rest then building.

1-chronicles-22:18:8.summary: “The Lord our God has given our brothers rest” echoes the rest formula.

1-chronicles-22:18:9.summary: “The Lord is with you” to Gideon echoes “Is not the Lord with you?”

1-chronicles-22:18:10.summary: Abigail’s blessing of David’s house has no specific link to rest.

1-chronicles-22:18:11.summary: The Lord “had given Israel rest from all their enemies all around,” the same formula.

1-chronicles-22:18:12.summary: The Lord fighting for Israel generally underlies the land’s subjugation.

1-chronicles-22:18:13.summary: The Lord fought for Israel to take the land, a general parallel.

1-chronicles-22:19:6.summary: The ark of the Lord’s covenant is brought into the house, fulfilling David’s instruction.

1-chronicles-22:19:1.summary: Seek the Lord “with all your heart and with all your soul,” matching the call to seek with hearts and souls.

1-chronicles-22:19:2.summary: “Seek the Lord” echoes the call to seek the Lord.

1-chronicles-22:19:3.summary: Seeking to dwell in the Lord’s house loosely links seeking and the temple.

1-chronicles-22:19:4.summary: David’s desire to build “a house for the name of the Lord God,” earlier in the same speech.

1-chronicles-22:19:5.summary: The priests bring the ark into the house’s inner sanctuary, fulfilling the charge.

1-chronicles-22:19:8.summary: Solomon placed there “the ark, in which is the Lord’s covenant,” fulfilling this instruction.

1-chronicles-22:19:9.summary: “Rise, be baptized” shares only the word “rise.”

1-chronicles-22:19:10.summary: David could not build because of wars until the Lord subdued them, explaining the charge to Solomon.

1-chronicles-22:19:11.summary: Moses urges heeding with the heart, a general exhortation parallel.

1-chronicles-22:19:12.summary: Jehoshaphat “set his face to seek the Lord,” a general seeking parallel.

1-chronicles-22:19:13.summary: Remaining with the Lord “with steadfast purpose of heart” loosely echoes giving hearts to seek Him.

1-chronicles-22:19:14.summary: Daniel sets his face to seek the Lord in prayer, a general seeking parallel.

1-chronicles-22:19:15.summary: Haggai’s call to set hearts on one’s ways relates loosely to temple rebuilding.

1-chronicles-22:19:16.summary: “Arise and act,” the same command in David’s earlier charge.

1-chronicles-23:1:0.summary: David died “full of days” and “Solomon his son reigned in his place,” the same wording.

1-chronicles-23:1:1.summary: God chose Solomon to sit on the throne over Israel, the succession recorded here.

1-chronicles-23:1:2.summary: David has Solomon anointed king to “reign in my place,” the parallel account (truncated).

1-chronicles-23:1:3.summary: “King David was old and advanced in days,” the same aged David at succession.

1-chronicles-23:1:5.summary: David vows Solomon “shall reign after me … in my place,” the same succession.

1-chronicles-23:1:6.summary: Abraham died “old and full of days,” the same idiom.

1-chronicles-23:1:7.summary: Job’s image of ripe grain gathered in season is too general.

1-chronicles-23:1:8.summary: Isaac died “old and full of days,” the same idiom.

1-chronicles-23:2:0.summary: David consults commanders of thousands and hundreds, a similar leadership assembly but not the same gathering of priests and Levites.
1-chronicles-23:2:0.why: Shows David's habit of convening leaders.

1-chronicles-23:2:2.summary: Joshua summons all Israel's elders and leaders, a similar national convocation formula with a different leader and occasion.
1-chronicles-23:2:2.why: Pattern of a leader's final assembly.

1-chronicles-23:2:3.summary: Joshua “gathered all the tribes of Israel” and their leaders, echoing David's gathering but a different event.
1-chronicles-23:2:3.why: Parallel convocation by an aging leader.

1-chronicles-23:2:4.summary: Josiah gathers elders, priests, and Levites to the Lord's house; similar assembly of the same groups, different king and purpose.
1-chronicles-23:2:4.why: Later royal assembly of the same orders.

1-chronicles-23:3:1.summary: Numbers 4 counts the Levites by age for tent service (Greek gives twenty-five years), the Mosaic precedent for David's Levite census.
1-chronicles-23:3:1.why: Background and age difference for Levite census.

1-chronicles-23:4:0.summary: Jehoshaphat appoints Levites and priests to judge in Jerusalem, a later instance of Levites serving as judges.

1-chronicles-23:4:1.summary: Moses commands appointing judges and recording officers in every city, a general basis for officials and judges.
1-chronicles-23:4:1.why: Legal basis for judges and officers.

1-chronicles-23:4:2.summary: Levites over vessels, flour, oil and loaves illustrate the kinds of temple work supervised, without the numbers or offices.

1-chronicles-23:4:3.summary: Joel is overseer over Benjaminites in Jerusalem; only the word “overseer” connects, with no Levite or temple-work link.

1-chronicles-23:4:4.summary: Chonenia's Levites are assigned outside labor “to act as scribes and give judgments,” specifying the 6,000 Levite scribes and judges.
1-chronicles-23:4:4.why: Shows who filled the scribe-judge role.

1-chronicles-23:4:5.summary: After the exile Levites are set “over those doing the work in the Lord's house,” echoing the supervisors over the house's works.
1-chronicles-23:4:5.why: Post-exile restoration of the same office.

1-chronicles-23:4:6.summary: Ozi is overseer of the Levites “opposite the work of the house of God,” a later Levite supervisory post.

1-chronicles-23:4:7.summary: Levites over the treasuries of the Lord's house belong to David's same Levite organization, but treasuries are not named in the source.

1-chronicles-23:4:8.summary: Levites “assigned to all the work of ministry” of God's house, a general statement of Levite duties.

1-chronicles-23:4:9.summary: Malachi speaks of priests guarding knowledge and law; no link to Levite supervisors, scribes, or judges counted by David.

1-chronicles-23:4:10.summary: Paul's charge to church overseers shares only the idea of oversight, not any Levite office or temple work.

1-chronicles-23:4:11.summary: Same chapter details the Levites' works of ministry in God's house, expanding the supervisory duties summarized in verse 4.
1-chronicles-23:4:11.why: Spells out what the supervisors oversaw.

1-chronicles-23:4:12.summary: Hard cases go to the Levitical priests and the judge, a general Levitical judicial role, not David's appointed judges.

1-chronicles-23:5:0.summary: Hezekiah stations Levites with cymbals and harps “according to the command of King David,” standing with “David's instruments.”
1-chronicles-23:5:0.why: Confirms David made the praise instruments.

1-chronicles-23:5:1.summary: Greek Psalm 86:7 reads “the dwelling in you is like that of all who rejoice”; it lacks the singers and players the label assumes.
1-chronicles-23:5:1.why: Greek wording does not carry the link.

1-chronicles-23:5:2.summary: Greek Amos 6:5 mentions “clapping to the sound of instruments” but not David devising instruments, so the specific link is absent.
1-chronicles-23:5:2.why: Greek wording does not carry the link.

1-chronicles-23:5:3.summary: Solomon stations Levites “to praise” and “the gatekeepers in their divisions at each gate” following David's commands.

1-chronicles-23:5:4.summary: Lists the Levite gatekeepers and their guard duties at the gates, the office counted at four thousand.
1-chronicles-23:5:4.why: Names and duties of the gatekeepers.

1-chronicles-23:5:5.summary: David's divisions of the gates among Korite and other Levite families detail the four thousand gatekeepers.

1-chronicles-23:5:6.summary: David has Levites appoint singers with harps, lyres and cymbals, plus gatekeepers, matching the praise and gatekeeping groups.

1-chronicles-23:5:7.summary: Kohathite and Korite Levites stand to praise the Lord loudly before battle, a later instance of Levite praise.
1-chronicles-23:5:7.why: Example of Levite praise in action.

1-chronicles-23:5:8.summary: Levite psalm singers work day and night, related to the praise group but without instruments or numbers.

1-chronicles-23:5:9.summary: Singers and gatekeepers return with Ezra, showing the same Levite orders persisting after the exile.

1-chronicles-23:5:10.summary: Abdedom and Ossa are named as gatekeepers before the ark, an individual instance of the gatekeeper office.

1-chronicles-23:5:12.summary: Asaph's singers and the gatekeepers serve “according to the commands of David” under Josiah, the same two Levite groups.

1-chronicles-23:5:13.summary: Gatekeepers and singers settle in their towns after the exile, a list naming the same orders without a specific link.

1-chronicles-23:5:14.summary: Solomon makes harps and lyres for the singers, related to instruments for praise but made by Solomon, not David.

1-chronicles-23:5:15.summary: David appoints Asaph, Aiman and Idithon's sons with kinyrai, nablai and cymbals, numbered head by head, to give thanks and praise.

1-chronicles-23:5:16.summary: David appoints singers who minister with instruments before the tent, the musicians counted among the four thousand.

1-chronicles-23:6:1.summary: Lists “Levi's sons: Gedson, Kaath, and Merari,” the same three names used for David's courses.

1-chronicles-23:6:4.summary: Repeats “Levi's sons: Gedson, Kaath, and Merari,” identical names to the division heads.

1-chronicles-23:6:0.summary: Solomon stations the priestly divisions and Levites at their watches “following David's ordinance,” implementing these courses.
1-chronicles-23:6:0.why: Shows David's divisions put into effect.

1-chronicles-23:6:2.summary: Levites stationed per King David's command, a general reference to David's ordering without the three family courses.

1-chronicles-23:6:3.summary: Post-exile priests and Levites are set in divisions and groups, a similar arrangement attributed to Moses' book.

1-chronicles-23:6:5.summary: The next chapter opens the parallel division of Aaron's sons, the priestly counterpart to the Levite courses.

1-chronicles-23:6:6.summary: Numbers lists the Levite clans of Gershon, Kohath and Merari, the same three family heads.
1-chronicles-23:6:6.why: Mosaic list of the same clans.

1-chronicles-23:6:7.summary: Under Josiah the Levites stand “in their divisions,” a later use of courses without naming the families.

1-chronicles-23:6:8.summary: Divisions of the gates among Korite families, a specific sub-division rather than the three-family organization.

1-chronicles-23:6:9.summary: Exodus names Levi's sons Gershon, Kohath and Merari and their sons, the foundational genealogy for the courses.

1-chronicles-23:6:10.summary: Hezekiah arranges divisions of priests and Levites, a later reorganization echoing David's courses.

1-chronicles-23:7:0.summary: Ladan's Gershonite house with ruler Jiiel matches Edan's line among the Gershonites here and in verse 8.

1-chronicles-23:7:1.summary: Gershon's sons Libni and Shimei; Shimei corresponds to Semei listed under the Gershonite line.

1-chronicles-23:7:2.summary: Gersam's sons led by Joel are Gershonites, related to the family but naming no Edan or Semei.

1-chronicles-23:7:3.summary: Gedson's sons “Lobeni and Semei” give the parallel Gershonite genealogy including Semei.

1-chronicles-23:8:0.summary: A Levite Jiiel appears among second-rank gatekeepers; same name, but identification with Edan's son is uncertain.

1-chronicles-23:8:1.summary: A Levite Joel is summoned by David for the ark; same name and era, identity with Edan's son uncertain.

1-chronicles-23:8:2.summary: Jiiel plays harps and lyres; the name matches, but identification with Edan's son is not shown.

1-chronicles-23:8:3.summary: This Joel is father of Heman, a Kohathite descended from Samuel, not the Gershonite Joel of Edan's line.

1-chronicles-23:8:4.summary: Joel “the ruler” of Gersam's (Gershonite) sons in David's day fits Joel of Edan's Gershonite house.
1-chronicles-23:8:4.why: Identifies Joel as a Gershonite leader.

1-chronicles-23:12:3.summary: Lists “Kaath's sons: Ambram, Issaar, Hebron, and Oziel,” the same four names.

1-chronicles-23:12:0.summary: Exodus names Kohath's sons Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel, the same four sons.

1-chronicles-23:12:1.summary: Numbers lists the Hebron clan and says Kohath begat Amram, giving only part of Kohath's four sons.

1-chronicles-23:12:2.summary: The Amramite, Izharite, Hebronite and Uzzielite divisions belong to Kohath, matching all four sons.

1-chronicles-23:13:0.summary: Amram fathers Aaron and Moses (and Miriam), the same sons named for Ambram.
1-chronicles-23:13:0.why: Birth record of Aaron and Moses.

1-chronicles-23:13:1.summary: Levitical priests are chosen to stand before the Lord and “to bless in His name,” matching ministering and invoking His name.

1-chronicles-23:13:2.summary: Aaron burns incense morning and evening “before the Lord,” the incense duty for which he was set apart.

1-chronicles-23:13:3.summary: God chose Aaron's house to serve as priests and “burn incense,” the same priestly privileges.

1-chronicles-23:13:4.summary: Lev 17 regulates where slaughter must occur; addressing Aaron's sons is incidental to his consecration for incense.

1-chronicles-23:13:5.summary: Korah's company and Aaron each offer incense, the test that later vindicates Aaron's exclusive right; only indirectly related.

1-chronicles-23:13:6.summary: Aaron and his sons bear responsibility for the priesthood, a general statement of their distinct office.

1-chronicles-23:13:7.summary: Aaron places incense and makes atonement for the people, an instance of his consecrated incense ministry.

1-chronicles-23:13:8.summary: Recipe for the most holy incense, related to incense but not to Aaron's consecration.

1-chronicles-23:13:9.summary: No one takes priestly honor himself but is called by God “just as Aaron was,” reflecting Aaron's being set apart.
1-chronicles-23:13:9.why: New Testament reading of Aaron's call.

1-chronicles-23:13:10.summary: Zechariah is chosen by lot “to burn incense” by priestly custom, continuing Aaron's line's duty generally.

1-chronicles-23:13:11.summary: Instructions to consecrate Aaron and his sons and the most holy things, the consecration referenced here.

1-chronicles-23:13:12.summary: Aaron is called “the Lord's holy one,” echoing his consecration as most holy.

1-chronicles-23:13:13.summary: “Burning incense belongs to the priests, Aaron's sons, who are sanctified to burn incense,” a close echo of verse 13.
1-chronicles-23:13:13.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

1-chronicles-23:13:14.summary: Moses and Aaron among His priests, those who “call on His name,” matching invoking His name.

1-chronicles-23:13:15.summary: The anointed priest after his father makes atonement, a general high-priestly succession theme.

1-chronicles-23:13:16.summary: The Amramite division of Kohath is named, but not Aaron, Moses, or the consecration.

1-chronicles-23:13:17.summary: Aaron and his sons bless Israel and “put My name upon” them, the blessing in His name assigned here.

1-chronicles-23:13:18.summary: Paul's being set apart from the womb shares only a general idea of separation, not Aaron's priestly consecration.

1-chronicles-23:13:19.summary: Aaron lifts his hands and blesses the people after offerings, an instance of priestly blessing.

1-chronicles-23:13:20.summary: Priests eat the most holy sin offering to make atonement; shares “most holy” but a different topic.

1-chronicles-23:13:21.summary: Aaron brings incense within the veil on the day of atonement, his most holy incense ministry.
1-chronicles-23:13:21.why: Highest act of Aaron's incense duty.

1-chronicles-23:13:22.summary: Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu offer unauthorized incense and die, a contrast to proper incense ministry.

1-chronicles-23:13:23.summary: God distinguishes Aaron's priesthood at the altar from the Levites who serve the tent, the same separation as verse 13.

1-chronicles-23:13:24.summary: Fire consumes the 250 offering incense and their fire pans become a sign; shown text implies the incense right but does not state it.
1-chronicles-23:13:24.why: Background on the exclusive incense right.

1-chronicles-23:13:25.summary: The Spirit's “set apart” of Barnabas and Saul shares only the notion of separation.

1-chronicles-23:13:26.summary: Priests are to “distinguish between the holy and the profane,” a related priestly function with incidental verbal overlap.

1-chronicles-23:13:27.summary: God will “consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests,” matching Aaron consecrated with his sons.

1-chronicles-23:13:29.summary: “Ambram's sons: Aaron, Moses, and Mariam,” the parallel genealogy in the same book.

1-chronicles-23:13:30.summary: Jochebed bore Aaron, Moses and Miriam to Amram, naming the same sons.

1-chronicles-23:13:31.summary: Paul “set apart for the gospel” shares only a general idea of being set apart.

1-chronicles-23:13:32.summary: An angel offers incense at the heavenly altar, a loose echo of incense ministry before God.

1-chronicles-23:13:33.summary: Aaron and his sons are anointed and sanctified with a priesthood “for ever, throughout their generations,” matching “he and his sons for ever.”

1-chronicles-23:14:0.summary: Moses is called “the man of God,” the same title used here.

1-chronicles-23:14:1.summary: “A prayer of Moses, the man of God” uses the same title.

1-chronicles-23:14:2.summary: Soubael, descendant of Gersam and Moses, and Eliezer's line show Moses' sons counted among the Levites.

1-chronicles-23:15:1.summary: Moses names his son Gershom, the Gersam listed here.

1-chronicles-23:15:2.summary: Moses takes his wife and children toward Egypt; the sons are implied but not named.

1-chronicles-23:16:1.summary: A Soubael leads the thirteenth musician course; the name matches, but identity with Gersam's son is not shown.

1-chronicles-23:16:2.summary: “Of Ambram's sons, Soubael” names the same Soubael in the Levite rosters.

1-chronicles-23:17:0.summary: For Eliezer, “Raabias a son” names the same Raabia descended from Eliezer.

1-chronicles-23:18:0.summary: “Of the Issari, Salomoth” names the same Izharite head.

1-chronicles-23:18:1.summary: A Salomoth is over the treasuries, but context links him to Eliezer's line, so identity with Issaar's son is uncertain.

1-chronicles-23:19:0.summary: The parallel list of Hebron's sons gives Amadia second, Jaziel third and Jokom fourth, matching this order.

1-chronicles-23:19:1.summary: Hebron's sons are led by Eliel, a different leader name for the same clan.

1-chronicles-23:21:3.summary: “Merari's sons: Mooli and Mousi” and “Of Mooli: Eleazar” and Kis parallel this list exactly.

1-chronicles-23:21:0.summary: Merari's sons Mahli and Mushi are the same Mooli and Mousi.

1-chronicles-23:21:2.summary: The shown text lists only Somea, Aggia and Asaia, with no Merari, Mooli or Mousi.
1-chronicles-23:21:2.why: No shared names in shown text.

1-chronicles-23:21:4.summary: This is a Gershonite line (Lobeni, Jeeth, Zemma), not Merari's sons.

1-chronicles-23:22:0.summary: “Eleazar died and had no sons,” repeating the same note about Mooli's son.

1-chronicles-23:22:1.summary: Daughters without brothers marry within their father's clan, the law behind Eleazar's daughters marrying Kis's sons.

1-chronicles-23:24:0.summary: Gershon and Merari carry the tent on the march, related to Levite work but not to the census.

1-chronicles-23:24:1.summary: Kohath carries the holy things on the march, a general Levite duty.

1-chronicles-23:24:2.summary: The same chapter counts Levites from thirty years, while this verse says twenty, with shared “head by head” wording.
1-chronicles-23:24:2.why: Highlights the change in age limit.

1-chronicles-23:24:3.summary: Levites enter service from twenty-five years in the Tent of Testimony, a different age threshold for the same ministry.

1-chronicles-23:24:4.summary: Levites “from twenty years old and upward” are set over the work in the Lord's house, the same age and duty.
1-chronicles-23:24:4.why: Post-exile adoption of David's age rule.

1-chronicles-23:24:5.summary: Levites enter tent work “from twenty-five years old and upward,” the Mosaic age precedent.

1-chronicles-23:24:6.summary: “By the number of their names, head by head... from twenty years old and upward” repeats the census formula.

1-chronicles-23:24:7.summary: Registration by ancestral houses, “counting their names, from twenty years old and upward... head by head.”

1-chronicles-23:24:8.summary: Levites registered “by their ancestral houses,” the Mosaic counterpart of numbering Levi's sons.
