1-chronicles-27:3:4.summary: Judah’s blessing as ruler gives general background to a Judahite leading the first division.

1-chronicles-27:4:0.summary: Eleazar, among the three mighty men, belongs to Dodia’s family in parallels, but Dodia is not named here.

1-chronicles-27:4:1.summary: “Eleazar son of Dodai the Achochi” links Dodia the Echochi, the same family.

1-chronicles-27:5:1.summary: “Banaias son of Jodae” over the Chereththi and Pheleththi, the same commander.

1-chronicles-27:5:0.summary: The shown text names Zadok, Abiathar, and Nathan’s sons, not Banaias.
1-chronicles-27:5:0.why: No link in the shown text.

1-chronicles-27:6:0.summary: Benaiah son of Jehoiada’s exploits and rank among the mighty explain Banaias being over the thirty.

1-chronicles-27:6:2.summary: David’s song of righteousness has no link to Banaias or the thirty.

1-chronicles-27:7:1.summary: “Asahel, Joab’s brother” among David’s mighty men, the same man.

1-chronicles-27:7:2.summary: Asahel, Joab’s brother, pursues Abner; the shown text is truncated before his death, explaining his son’s role.

1-chronicles-27:8:0.summary: “Sammoth the Adite” among David’s mighty men matches Samaoth here.

1-chronicles-27:8:1.summary: “Shammah the Aroudite” in David’s mighty men may be Samaoth the Jesrae, but name and clan differ in the Saints text.

1-chronicles-27:8:2.summary: The Issari Levites as scribes and judges have no link to Samaoth “the Jesrae” beyond a similar-sounding clan name.

1-chronicles-27:9:0.summary: “Son of Ekkes the Thekoite” matches Odouias son of Ekkes the Thekoite, though the given name is spelled Orai.
1-chronicles-27:9:0.why: Identifies this commander among the mighty men.

1-chronicles-27:9:1.summary: “Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite” is the same Thekoite son of Ekkes among David’s mighty men.
1-chronicles-27:9:1.why: Identifies this commander among the mighty men.

1-chronicles-27:10:0.summary: “Chelles the Phelonite” among the mighty men matches Chelles from Phallous.
1-chronicles-27:10:0.why: Identifies this commander among the mighty men.

1-chronicles-27:10:1.summary: “Elles the Phelothite” is the same Chelles from Phallous, spelled differently.
1-chronicles-27:10:1.why: Identifies this commander among the mighty men.

1-chronicles-27:11:0.summary: “Sebocha the Astatothite” who killed a descendant of Rapha is Sobochai the Isathi.

1-chronicles-27:11:1.summary: “Sobochai the Asothite” among the mighty men is the same Sobochai.
1-chronicles-27:11:1.why: Identifies this commander among the mighty men.

1-chronicles-27:11:2.summary: The “clan of Zerah” of Judah is the clan called “the Zarai” here.

1-chronicles-27:12:1.summary: “Abiezer the Anathothite” among the mighty men is the same Abiezer from Anathoth.
1-chronicles-27:12:1.why: Identifies this commander among the mighty men.

1-chronicles-27:13:0.summary: “Moorai the Netophathite” is Meera from Netouphat, spelled differently.
1-chronicles-27:13:0.why: Identifies this commander among the mighty men.

1-chronicles-27:13:1.summary: “Moore the Netophathite” is the same Meera from Netouphat.
1-chronicles-27:13:1.why: Identifies this commander among the mighty men.

1-chronicles-27:14:0.summary: “Banaias the Pharathonite” is the same Banaias from Pharathon.
1-chronicles-27:14:0.why: Identifies this commander among the mighty men.

1-chronicles-27:14:1.summary: “Benaiah the Pirathonite” is Banaias from Pharathon in another spelling.
1-chronicles-27:14:1.why: Identifies this commander among the mighty men.

1-chronicles-27:15:0.summary: “Ela son of Baanah the Netophathite” shares the Netophathite origin, but the name differs from Choldai.

1-chronicles-27:15:1.summary: Othniel, Caleb’s younger brother and judge, is the Gothoniel whose clan Choldai belonged to.

1-chronicles-27:15:2.summary: Othniel son of Kenaz is the ancestor called Gothoniel here.

1-chronicles-27:15:3.summary: “Cholod son of Nooza the Netophathite” matches Choldai the Netophati.
1-chronicles-27:15:3.why: Identifies this commander among the mighty men.

1-chronicles-27:17:0.summary: An Asabias of the Chebroni oversaw Transjordan; possibly this Asabias, though his father is not given there.

1-chronicles-27:17:1.summary: “Sadok, a young man mighty in strength” appears with the “leader for Aaron,” the same Sadok over Aaron here.

1-chronicles-27:17:2.summary: Eleazar’s priestly houses are divided; general priestly organization with no named link.

1-chronicles-27:17:3.summary: Sadok presides at the Levites’ lots before the king, the same priestly leader over Aaron.

1-chronicles-27:18:1.summary: Eliab, Jesse’s eldest seen by Samuel, is “one of David’s brethren” named here.

1-chronicles-27:21:0.summary: Abner’s death at Joab’s hand concerns the father of Asiel son of Abenner.

1-chronicles-27:21:1.summary: Ahinadab in Mahanaim has no stated link to Galaad or to Jaddai or Asiel in the shown text.
1-chronicles-27:21:1.why: No link in the shown text.

1-chronicles-27:21:2.summary: Names “Abner son of Ner,” father of Asiel son of Abenner.

1-chronicles-27:21:3.summary: Identifies “Abner son of Ner” as Saul’s commander, the Abenner whose son led Benjamin.

1-chronicles-27:22:0.summary: David assembles “all Israel’s rulers,” which would include these tribal heads, though they are not named.

1-chronicles-27:23:1.summary: Descendants “as many as the stars of heaven” echoes the Lord’s promise to multiply Israel like the stars.

1-chronicles-27:23:2.summary: The Mosaic census counted “from twenty years old and upward,” the same age line David observed.

1-chronicles-27:23:3.summary: David orders Joab to “number Israel,” the same census referred to here.

1-chronicles-27:24:0.summary: Joab’s census for David and the Lord’s anger against Israel are the same event; the shown text is truncated.
1-chronicles-27:24:0.why: Fuller account of the census and wrath.

1-chronicles-27:25:0.summary: The Saints text speaks of “fortified cities” for Pharaoh, not storehouses, so the assumed link is absent.
1-chronicles-27:25:0.why: Greek wording lacks the assumed link.

1-chronicles-27:25:1.summary: Joseph stores food in the cities of Egypt; a general parallel to royal storehouses.

1-chronicles-27:25:2.summary: Men have “stores in the countryside,” similar wording but an unrelated incident.

1-chronicles-27:25:3.summary: Hezekiah empties “the treasuries of the king’s house,” the same kind of royal treasury.

1-chronicles-27:25:4.summary: Asa takes gold from the treasuries of the king’s house; same royal treasuries in a later scene.

1-chronicles-27:25:5.summary: Uzziah builds “towers” and keeps herds and vinedressers, a royal estate like David’s towers and storehouses.

1-chronicles-27:28:0.summary: “Sycamores in the plain” names the same royal tree crop overseen here.
1-chronicles-27:28:0.why: Same sycamore groves of the plain.

1-chronicles-27:28:1.summary: “Sycamores in the plain” matches the groves Balanas oversaw.
1-chronicles-27:28:1.why: Same sycamore groves of the plain.

1-chronicles-27:28:2.summary: Solomon’s officers provisioned the king, a general parallel to David’s overseers of produce.

1-chronicles-27:28:3.summary: Israel camped like two flocks of goats; nothing concerns olives, sycamores, or oil stores.

1-chronicles-27:29:0.summary: Mentions pasture around “Sharon,” the region implied by Satrais “the Sharonite.”

1-chronicles-27:29:1.summary: A valley as “a resting place for cattle” loosely recalls cattle in the valleys.

1-chronicles-27:30:0.summary: Job’s wealth in camels and donkeys parallels royal herds only generally.

1-chronicles-27:30:1.summary: Pharaoh offers the best land; the shown text mentions no livestock or overseers.
1-chronicles-27:30:1.why: No link in the shown text.

1-chronicles-27:31:0.summary: War against “resident aliens” in Galaad does not name the Agarites in the Saints text.
1-chronicles-27:31:0.why: Greek wording lacks the assumed link.

1-chronicles-27:32:0.summary: “Son of Achamani” is shared with Jiiel here; perhaps the same family, otherwise unrelated.

1-chronicles-27:32:1.summary: Jonadab, David’s nephew, was “very shrewd,” loosely like Jonathan the understanding counselor; different person.

1-chronicles-27:32:2.summary: A Jonathan of David’s family appears, but as nephew, not “paternal uncle”; identity uncertain.

1-chronicles-27:33:0.summary: Hushai, “David’s companion,” is Chousi, “the king’s first friend.”
1-chronicles-27:33:0.why: Shows Chousi’s role in Absalom’s revolt.

1-chronicles-27:33:2.summary: Hushai the Archite, “David’s companion,” meets David in grief; the same friend Chousi.

1-chronicles-27:33:3.summary: Absalom calls Hushai David’s “companion,” the same friend named here.

1-chronicles-27:33:4.summary: A prophecy against shepherds and a “fellow citizen” has no specific link to David’s counselors.

1-chronicles-27:33:5.summary: A betraying “leader and acquaintance” may evoke Achitophel, but he is not named in the shown text.
1-chronicles-27:33:5.why: Possible echo of a betraying counselor.
1-chronicles-27:33:5.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

1-chronicles-27:33:6.summary: Ahithophel, the king’s counselor, hangs himself after his counsel fails.

1-chronicles-27:33:7.summary: Ahithophel’s counsel was regarded like God’s word, explaining his role as “the king’s counselor.”

1-chronicles-27:34:0.summary: Joab and Abiathar the priest side with Adonijah, the same two officials listed here.

1-chronicles-27:34:1.summary: Joab son of Sarouia becomes “ruler and general,” explaining his post as chief commander.

1-chronicles-27:34:2.summary: Banaias son of Jodae leads the third division; Jodae son of Banaiou belongs to the same family.

1-chronicles-27:18:0.summary: 1 Samuel 17:29 has no corresponding passage in this edition, which follows the Greek text; there is no Saints reading to compare.
1-chronicles-27:18:0.why: Compare a Hebrew-based translation if this passage matters for study.
1-chronicles-27:18:0.note: Passage unavailable in this edition; the review records the absence rather than an interpretation.

1-chronicles-27:18:2.summary: 1 Samuel 17:13 has no corresponding passage in this edition, which follows the Greek text; there is no Saints reading to compare.
1-chronicles-27:18:2.why: Compare a Hebrew-based translation if this passage matters for study.
1-chronicles-27:18:2.note: Passage unavailable in this edition; the review records the absence rather than an interpretation.

1-chronicles-28:1:0.summary: David “gathered all Israel’s rulers,” the same kind of assembly convened here.

1-chronicles-28:1:1.summary: Lists David’s mighty men, likely among the “powerful men” summoned here; shown text is truncated.

1-chronicles-28:1:3.summary: Aging Joshua summons Israel’s leaders, scribes, and judges, as David assembles rulers for his farewell charge.

1-chronicles-28:1:4.summary: Joshua gathers elders, scribes, and judges before God, paralleling David’s final assembly.

1-chronicles-28:2:0.summary: “Footstool of My feet,” “house,” and “My rest” echo David’s house of rest and standing place for the Lord’s feet.

1-chronicles-28:2:1.summary: Worship “at His footstool” matches the ark as “a standing place for our Lord’s feet.”

1-chronicles-28:2:3.summary: God forgets “His footstool” in anger, the same image of His feet’s resting place, now judged.

1-chronicles-28:2:4.summary: “Brothers” and “in the midst of the assembly” echo David’s address only verbally.

1-chronicles-28:2:5.summary: David vows to find “a dwelling for the God of Jacob,” “where His feet stood,” and calls the ark to “Thy rest.”

1-chronicles-28:2:6.summary: David gathers bronze and treasures later used for the temple; general background to his preparations.

1-chronicles-28:2:7.summary: The ark “came to rest” under David, loosely matching the “house of rest for the ark.”

1-chronicles-28:2:8.summary: David bows on his bed at Solomon’s accession; nothing matches David standing to address the assembly.

1-chronicles-28:2:9.summary: David notes the ark “remains inside the tent,” the original desire to build it a house.

1-chronicles-28:2:10.summary: Israel calls David “your bones and your flesh,” loosely like David calling them “brethren.”
1-chronicles-28:2:10.why: King as brother to the people.

1-chronicles-28:2:11.summary: The king’s heart should not be lifted “above his brethren,” loosely reflected in David’s “brethren.”

1-chronicles-28:2:12.summary: The king is to be one “from among your brethren”; loosely reflected in David’s address.

1-chronicles-28:2:13.summary: Stephen quotes “footstool of My feet” and “place … for My rest,” the same house-and-rest language.
1-chronicles-28:2:13.why: New Testament reflection on God’s house.

1-chronicles-28:2:14.summary: “To my brothers; in the midst of the assembly” echoes David’s address only verbally.

1-chronicles-28:2:15.summary: Jacob sits up on his bed; no link to David standing before the assembly in the Saints text.

1-chronicles-28:2:16.summary: David “prepared” stones, iron, bronze, and cedar for God’s house, the preparations he mentions here.

1-chronicles-28:2:17.summary: “I have prepared for the Lord’s house” gold, silver, and more, matching David’s claim here.

1-chronicles-28:2:18.summary: “It came into the heart of my father David to build a house,” echoing “It came upon my heart to build.”

1-chronicles-28:2:19.summary: God calls Zion “My rest,” matching the “house of rest” David planned for the ark.

1-chronicles-28:3:1.summary: “You shall not build Me a house” is the original word David recalls here.

1-chronicles-28:3:2.summary: David “could not build a house … because of the wars,” matching the reason given here.

1-chronicles-28:3:3.summary: “You will not build the house; your son … will build,” the same divine refusal.
1-chronicles-28:3:3.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

1-chronicles-28:3:4.summary: “You will not build Me a house” in Nathan’s oracle, the word David recalls; shown text truncated.

1-chronicles-28:4:0.summary: God sends Samuel to Jesse, having seen “one among his sons to reign,” the choice David recalls.

1-chronicles-28:4:3.summary: “I took you from the sheepfold to be ruler over My people,” the choice and promise recalled here.

1-chronicles-28:4:4.summary: David asks that God’s word about his house be secure “for ever,” matching kingship “for ever” here.

1-chronicles-28:4:5.summary: David asks God to bless his house “for ever,” echoing his kingship over Israel for ever.

1-chronicles-28:4:6.summary: “A ruler shall not fail from Judah” grounds God choosing “the royal power in Judah.”

1-chronicles-28:4:7.summary: The Lord takes pleasure in those who fear Him; the Saints text here says “He was willing,” not “pleasure.”

1-chronicles-28:4:8.summary: “Judah is My king” matches God choosing royal power in Judah.

1-chronicles-28:4:9.summary: The Ziphites betray David’s hiding place; nothing concerns God’s choice of David as king.

1-chronicles-28:4:10.summary: “He desired me” loosely echoes God being “willing” that David become king.

1-chronicles-28:4:11.summary: The Lord sprang “from Judah,” loosely linked to God choosing Judah’s royal house.

1-chronicles-28:4:12.summary: “He chose Judah’s tribe” and “chose David His servant,” the same twofold choice David describes.

1-chronicles-28:4:13.summary: “I raised a chosen one … I found David My servant,” anointed with holy oil; shown text truncated.

1-chronicles-28:4:14.summary: “Judah is My king” matches God choosing the royal power in Judah.

1-chronicles-28:5:1.summary: Lists David’s many sons, including Solomon, the “many sons” mentioned here; shown text truncated.

1-chronicles-28:5:2.summary: God names Solomon and sets “the throne of his kingdom in Israel for ever,” the choice David reports.

1-chronicles-28:5:3.summary: God promises to secure the son “in My house and in his kingdom” and his throne for ever.

1-chronicles-28:5:4.summary: A son given rules “upon the throne of David,” a messianic extension of the throne theme.

1-chronicles-28:5:5.summary: Names David’s sons born in Jerusalem, including Solomon, the “many sons” here.

1-chronicles-28:5:6.summary: A psalm “For Solomon” prays for the king’s son; general royal theme.

1-chronicles-28:5:7.summary: “Solomon my son, the one whom the Lord has chosen,” repeats the choice stated here.

1-chronicles-28:5:8.summary: Solomon “sat upon the throne,” fulfilling God’s choice to seat him on the throne.

1-chronicles-28:5:9.summary: Solomon says God made him king in David’s place, acknowledging the choice David reports.

1-chronicles-28:5:10.summary: “Thou didst choose me as king of Thy people,” Solomon’s own echo of his election.

1-chronicles-28:6:0.summary: “He will build Me a house … I will be a father to him, and he will be a son,” the promise David repeats.

1-chronicles-28:6:1.summary: Christ as “a Son over His house” loosely echoes the son who builds God’s house.

1-chronicles-28:6:3.summary: “They shall certainly not enter My rest” has no link to Solomon building the house.

1-chronicles-28:6:4.summary: A man named Rising “will build the Lord’s house,” a later figure echoing the builder theme.

1-chronicles-28:6:6.summary: The builder of a house has honor; loosely related to the son who builds God’s house.

1-chronicles-28:6:7.summary: Solomon asks God to confirm His word to David; general link to the promise about Solomon.

1-chronicles-28:6:8.summary: “Thou didst tell me to build a temple,” Solomon’s own account of the commission given here.

1-chronicles-28:7:0.summary: Success depends “if you take care to do the ordinances and judgments,” with “be strong,” the same condition.

1-chronicles-28:7:1.summary: “Keeping His commandments, as it is this day” echoes “observe My commandments … as on this day.”

1-chronicles-28:7:2.summary: “Be strong … to keep and do” the commands parallels remaining strong to observe commandments.

1-chronicles-28:7:4.summary: “Be strong and act” to build; similar wording but a charge to build rather than obey.

1-chronicles-28:7:6.summary: “If your sons keep My covenant … they will sit for ever on your throne,” the same conditional promise.
1-chronicles-28:7:6.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

1-chronicles-28:7:7.summary: If Solomon keeps God’s “ordinances and commandments,” his throne will stand for ever.
1-chronicles-28:7:7.why: God restates the condition to Solomon.

1-chronicles-28:7:8.summary: Solomon’s heart was “not whole with the Lord,” failing the condition set here.

1-chronicles-28:7:9.summary: “If his sons … do not keep My commandments,” the Davidic promise’s condition; shown text truncated.

1-chronicles-28:7:10.summary: God sets up a kingdom that will stand for ever; general eternal-kingdom theme.

1-chronicles-28:7:11.summary: Because Solomon “has not kept My commandments,” the kingdom is torn away, the consequence of breaking this condition.
1-chronicles-28:7:11.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

1-chronicles-28:8:1.summary: Keep the commandments to prosper “upon the land which you shall inherit,” the same charge.

1-chronicles-28:8:2.summary: The Saints text says creatures were counted and “none sought another”; no seeking of commandments.
1-chronicles-28:8:2.why: Greek wording lacks the assumed link.

1-chronicles-28:8:3.summary: A good man’s inheritance to “children’s children” loosely echoes passing the land to sons.

1-chronicles-28:8:4.summary: Receiving and seeking commandment and wisdom loosely parallels “observe and seek all the commandments.”

1-chronicles-28:8:5.summary: “Eat the good things of the land and bequeath it to your sons for ever” closely echoes this verse.

1-chronicles-28:8:6.summary: Israel’s leaders stand “before the Lord,” loosely like the assembly before God here.

1-chronicles-28:8:7.summary: “Keep and do them” before the nations; general call to obedience.

1-chronicles-28:8:8.summary: A cloud of witnesses and running the race has no specific link to this charge.

1-chronicles-28:8:9.summary: God’s commandments “to be kept diligently”; general call to obedience.

1-chronicles-28:8:10.summary: Keeping God’s law “for ever”; general obedience theme.

1-chronicles-28:8:11.summary: A son urged to keep his father’s words; loosely like David charging Solomon.

1-chronicles-28:8:12.summary: Seeking God and not straying from His commandments; general parallel to “seek all the commandments.”

1-chronicles-28:8:13.summary: Covenant made with those present and future “before the Lord,” loosely like obligations passed to sons.

1-chronicles-28:8:14.summary: The Bereans examining Scripture shares nothing specific with this charge.

1-chronicles-28:8:15.summary: Shining as lights holding the word of life has no specific link here.

1-chronicles-28:8:16.summary: Letting light shine before people has no specific link to keeping commandments to inherit the land.

1-chronicles-28:8:17.summary: A prayer to “seek” God’s ordinances and “keep” His law loosely echoes “observe and seek all the commandments.”

1-chronicles-28:8:18.summary: “All here before God to hear everything the Lord has commanded” loosely echoes the assembly “in the ears of our God.”

1-chronicles-28:8:19.summary: Disobedience means perishing from the land Israel was to “inherit,” the reverse of the promise here.

1-chronicles-28:8:20.summary: A prayer for understanding of God’s ordinances; general obedience theme.

1-chronicles-28:9:7.summary: Azariah’s message to Asa repeats almost verbatim “If you seek Him, He shall be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you.”
1-chronicles-28:9:7.why: Shows David’s charge reused as a standing prophetic formula.

1-chronicles-28:9:0.summary: Both promise that God is found by those who seek Him with the “whole heart.”
1-chronicles-28:9:0.why: Prophetic restatement of the seek-and-find promise.

1-chronicles-28:9:1.summary: James urges drawing near to God and purifying divided hearts, loosely echoing wholehearted service and God’s responsiveness.
1-chronicles-28:9:1.why: New Testament call to undivided devotion.

1-chronicles-28:9:2.summary: Jesus’ “seek, and you will find” echoes the promise that the one who seeks God will find Him, but in a general sense.
1-chronicles-28:9:2.why: Gospel form of the seeking promise.

1-chronicles-28:9:3.summary: Isaiah calls to “Seek God” and find Him, and to forsake wicked ways and return, paralleling seek/find and forsake.
1-chronicles-28:9:3.why: Adds the call to repentance to the seeking promise.

1-chronicles-28:9:4.summary: God gives a heart “to know Me,” and the people return “from their whole heart,” matching knowing God with a whole heart.
1-chronicles-28:9:4.why: Shows God enabling the wholehearted knowledge David demands.

1-chronicles-28:9:5.summary: Solomon himself prays that hearts be “complete toward the Lord,” answering David’s charge to serve with a whole heart.
1-chronicles-28:9:5.why: Solomon’s later echo of his father’s charge.

1-chronicles-28:9:6.summary: A father instructs his son that seeking wisdom leads to “find the knowledge of God,” paralleling David’s seek-and-know charge to Solomon.
1-chronicles-28:9:6.why: Wisdom form of father-to-son instruction on knowing God.

1-chronicles-28:9:8.summary: Those who “know Thy name” trust because God has “not abandoned those who seek Thee,” combining knowing, seeking, and not forsaking.
1-chronicles-28:9:8.why: Psalmist’s confidence in the promise to seekers.

1-chronicles-28:9:10.summary: Worship “in spirit and truth” loosely parallels serving God with a whole heart and willing soul.

1-chronicles-28:9:11.summary: “I, the Lord, examine hearts” matches “the Lord examines every heart.”

1-chronicles-28:9:12.summary: God understands “my reasonings from afar,” paralleling that He “knows every thought.”
1-chronicles-28:9:12.why: Personal expression of God’s knowledge of thoughts.

1-chronicles-28:9:13.summary: God takes no pleasure in one who “draws back,” loosely like forsaking God and being forsaken.

1-chronicles-28:9:14.summary: Boasting in “knowing that I am the Lord” shares only the general theme of knowing God.
1-chronicles-28:9:14.why: Defines what true knowledge of God is.

1-chronicles-28:9:15.summary: Hosea laments “no recognition of God” in the land, the opposite of David’s charge to know God.
1-chronicles-28:9:15.why: Shows the failure David warns against.

1-chronicles-28:9:16.summary: Eternal life defined as knowing “the only true God” shares the general theme of knowing God.
1-chronicles-28:9:16.why: New Testament weight on knowing God.

1-chronicles-28:9:17.summary: David again says God “examinest hearts” and prays for “Solomon my son” to have a good heart for His commandments.
1-chronicles-28:9:17.why: David’s prayer completing his charge to Solomon.

1-chronicles-28:9:18.summary: The new-covenant promise that all will “know Me” shares only the theme of knowing the Lord.

1-chronicles-28:9:19.summary: God did not tell Jacob’s offspring to “Seek a futile thing,” implying seeking Him is fruitful; a loose link.
1-chronicles-28:9:19.why: Affirms seeking God is not vain.

1-chronicles-28:9:20.summary: Hezekiah walked before God “with a full heart,” an example of the wholehearted service David urges.

1-chronicles-28:9:21.summary: Shares only the phrase-type “God of my father” with “God of your fathers.”

1-chronicles-28:9:22.summary: Jeremiah defines knowing God as justice for the poor, sharing only the theme of knowing God.

1-chronicles-28:9:23.summary: At the same assembly the people offer eagerly “with a full heart,” fulfilling the call to serve with whole heart and willing soul.
1-chronicles-28:9:23.why: Shows the charge enacted in the same scene.

1-chronicles-28:9:24.summary: God warns Solomon that if he turns away, Israel will be removed “because they abandoned the Lord,” spelling out being forsaken.
1-chronicles-28:9:24.why: God’s own version of the warning to Solomon.

1-chronicles-28:9:25.summary: Solomon confesses “Thou alone knowest the hearts of all,” echoing that the Lord examines every heart.
1-chronicles-28:9:25.why: Solomon’s prayer applies his father’s teaching.

1-chronicles-28:9:26.summary: Acts speaks of overlooked times of ignorance and repentance; it shares no specific element with the verse.

1-chronicles-28:9:27.summary: Nothing is hidden and all is “laid open to His eyes,” broadly matching God knowing every heart and thought.

1-chronicles-28:9:28.summary: The psalmist walked “in innocence of my heart,” loosely like serving God with a whole heart.

1-chronicles-28:9:29.summary: God “who tests hearts and kidneys” matches the Lord examining every heart.
1-chronicles-28:9:29.why: Psalm formula for God searching the heart.

1-chronicles-28:9:30.summary: God says “I know their wickedness” before they enter the land, a loose parallel to God knowing thoughts.

1-chronicles-28:9:31.summary: Josiah walked in David’s ways without turning aside, a general example of faithful service.

1-chronicles-28:9:32.summary: “Serve God acceptably” shares only the general idea of serving God.

1-chronicles-28:9:33.summary: Job contrasts those who “listen and serve” with those who “do not wish to know the Lord,” a loose thematic echo.

1-chronicles-28:9:34.summary: The apostles pray to the Lord “who knowest everyone’s heart,” echoing that the Lord examines every heart.

1-chronicles-28:9:35.summary: Those who refuse to retain God in knowledge are handed over, loosely like forsaking God and being forsaken.

1-chronicles-28:9:36.summary: Peter’s “Thou knowest all things” touches only the general idea of God knowing the heart.

1-chronicles-28:9:37.summary: Jesus “knew what was within a person,” paralleling God knowing every heart in a general way.

1-chronicles-28:9:38.summary: Moses’ aim “that you might know that the Lord your God, He is God” shares only the theme of knowing God.

1-chronicles-28:9:39.summary: “Because you thrust away recognition, I too will thrust you away” mirrors the reciprocal “forsake Him, He will forsake you.”

1-chronicles-28:9:40.summary: God shines in hearts to give “the knowledge of the glory of God,” a general link to knowing God.

1-chronicles-28:9:41.summary: God observes that man’s mind is bent on evil, loosely relating to God knowing human thoughts.

1-chronicles-28:9:42.summary: The Lord “who tests kidneys and hearts” parallels the Lord examining every heart.

1-chronicles-28:9:43.summary: As metal is tested, “so hearts are chosen before the Lord,” matching God examining hearts.

1-chronicles-28:9:44.summary: God’s hand is good “upon all who seek Him” but against “all who abandon Him,” the same two-way principle.

1-chronicles-28:9:45.summary: God exposes the evil “words” rising in Gog’s heart, only loosely like God knowing thoughts.

1-chronicles-28:9:46.summary: Shares only the formula “the God of your fathers.”

1-chronicles-28:9:47.summary: A psalm of God as refuge and helper has no specific link to knowing, serving, or seeking God here.

1-chronicles-28:9:48.summary: “Understanding kidneys and hearts” echoes God examining every heart and knowing every thought.

1-chronicles-28:9:49.summary: Israel “shall forsake Me” and God “will forsake them,” the same reciprocal warning.

1-chronicles-28:9:50.summary: Jesus discerns Nathanael’s guileless heart, only loosely like God knowing hearts.

1-chronicles-28:9:51.summary: Solomon recalls David walking in “uprightness of heart,” connecting the same father and son but not the specific charge.

1-chronicles-28:9:52.summary: Jesus contrasts not knowing God with knowing Him and keeping His word; only a general theme.

1-chronicles-28:9:53.summary: The altar “To an unknown god” shares only incidental words about knowing.

1-chronicles-28:9:54.summary: Christ is the One “who searcheth kidneys and hearts,” echoing the Lord examining every heart.

1-chronicles-28:9:55.summary: “Those abandoning the Lord will be brought to an end” matches being forsaken utterly for forsaking Him.

1-chronicles-28:9:56.summary: Shares only the title “God of Abraham your father.”

1-chronicles-28:9:57.summary: The king calling God “my Father” has no specific link to this charge.

1-chronicles-28:9:58.summary: Shepherding “willingly” touches only the idea of a willing soul in service.

1-chronicles-28:9:59.summary: God sees that each one set his heart on evil, loosely like God knowing every thought.

1-chronicles-28:9:60.summary: Readiness making a gift acceptable loosely echoes a “willing soul.”

1-chronicles-28:9:61.summary: Some “have no knowledge of God,” sharing only the theme of knowing God.

1-chronicles-28:9:62.summary: Giving “not out of compulsion” loosely echoes a willing soul.

1-chronicles-28:9:63.summary: Solomon prays that peoples “may know Thy name,” sharing only the theme of knowing God.
1-chronicles-28:9:63.why: Knowledge of God extended to nations.

1-chronicles-28:10:1.summary: Paul’s advice to Timothy about teaching shares no specific element with the charge to build the sanctuary.

1-chronicles-28:11:0.summary: In the same scene David gives Solomon everything in writing for “carrying out the pattern.”

1-chronicles-28:11:6.summary: The Rechabites brought into a court of the Lord’s house share only incidental wording.

1-chronicles-28:11:7.summary: Gives the measurements “when Solomon began building God’s house,” the realization of the pattern David handed over.

1-chronicles-28:11:8.summary: Side chambers built around the house loosely correspond to the rooms in David’s pattern.

1-chronicles-28:11:19.summary: Levites over “the treasuries of the Lord’s house” loosely match the storerooms named in the pattern (truncated).

1-chronicles-28:11:24.summary: The tabernacle work done “as the Lord commanded Moses” loosely parallels building to a given pattern.

1-chronicles-28:11:25.summary: The inner sanctuary made into the Holy of Holies for the ark loosely matches the house of propitiation.

1-chronicles-28:12:7.summary: “According to the pattern shown to you” is the tabernacle precedent for David’s revealed pattern.

1-chronicles-28:12:8.summary: God calling Bezalel for the tabernacle work is only generally related to the temple plan.

1-chronicles-28:12:9.summary: Salomoth was over “the treasuries of the holy things” consecrated for God’s house, matching the storerooms of the holy things.

1-chronicles-28:15:6.summary: Zechariah’s olive trees beside the lampstand share only the lampstand image.

1-chronicles-28:16:2.summary: Solomon makes ten tables and golden bowls, matching the golden tables in David’s plan.

1-chronicles-28:17:0.summary: A priest’s “meat hook” at Shiloh shares only the implement named in the list.

1-chronicles-28:17:1.summary: Silver dishes and bowls given by weight for the altar loosely parallel weighed sanctuary vessels.

1-chronicles-28:17:2.summary: Solomon’s gold vessels and basins share only the theme of gold vessels, and they are palace vessels.

1-chronicles-28:17:3.summary: Solomon makes the bowls, incense cups, and fire pans “of pure gold,” realizing the golden vessels listed.

1-chronicles-28:18:4.summary: “Thou who sittest upon the cherubim” shares the cherubim throne image generally.

1-chronicles-28:18:5.summary: Solomon makes two cherubim with outspread wings in the inner sanctuary, realizing the cherubim in David’s pattern (truncated).

1-chronicles-28:18:7.summary: Solomon places “the gold altar” in the Lord’s house, matching the altar of tested gold in the plan.

1-chronicles-28:18:11.summary: Ezekiel’s wheels beside living creatures share only general chariot-throne imagery (truncated).

1-chronicles-28:19:3.summary: The tabernacle is erected “according to the plan shown,” paralleling the divinely given temple pattern.

1-chronicles-28:19:4.summary: “The Lord’s hand came upon me” shares only the Lord’s-hand phrase.

1-chronicles-28:19:5.summary: “The Lord’s hand came upon me” shares only the Lord’s-hand phrase.

1-chronicles-28:20:9.summary: Earlier in the speech David told Solomon “Be strong and act,” repeated here.

1-chronicles-28:21:0.summary: The priestly divisions organized by David are the “service courses of the priests” said to be ready (truncated).

1-chronicles-29:1:1.summary: Solomon calls himself “a little child,” confirming David’s description of him as young and tender.

1-chronicles-29:1:2.summary: Rehoboam is called “younger and cowardly in heart,” a different king sharing only youth.

1-chronicles-29:1:5.summary: David assembled Israel’s rulers in Jerusalem, the assembly now addressed.

1-chronicles-29:1:6.summary: David speaks “before the whole assembly of the Lord,” the same gathering.

1-chronicles-29:9:2.summary: Hearts “complete toward the Lord” loosely echoes offering with a full heart.

1-chronicles-29:9:3.summary: Joy “made full” shares only the joy theme.

1-chronicles-29:9:4.summary: Paul “rejoiced greatly” at the Philippians’ gifts, echoing David’s joy at generous giving.

1-chronicles-29:9:6.summary: Calling believers “my joy and crown” shares only the word joy.

1-chronicles-29:9:7.summary: “If the readiness is present, it is acceptable” loosely parallels eager giving.

1-chronicles-29:9:8.summary: The Greek-based psalm speaks of rule and begetting, not a willing people, so the link fails here.

1-chronicles-29:9:9.summary: Giving “according to the ability of your hand” and rejoicing before the Lord loosely parallels joyful giving.

1-chronicles-29:9:10.summary: Rejoicing over a found sheep shares only the word rejoice.

1-chronicles-29:9:11.summary: Paul’s joy over the Thessalonians’ faith shares only the joy theme.

1-chronicles-29:9:12.summary: The Saints text speaks of “mighty ones” blessing the Lord, lacking the volunteering idea the link assumes.

1-chronicles-29:9:13.summary: A father gladdened by a wise son has no specific link to this joyful offering.

1-chronicles-29:10:0.summary: “Blessed be the God and Father” shares the blessing formula and the address of God as Father.

1-chronicles-29:10:1.summary: “Blessed be the God and Father” shares the blessing formula and Father title.

1-chronicles-29:10:2.summary: Heavenly praise ascribing power, glory, and blessing shares only general doxology.

1-chronicles-29:10:3.summary: A greeting from “God our Father” shares only the Father title.

1-chronicles-29:10:4.summary: Glory to God “for the ages of ages” shares the eternal doxology theme.

1-chronicles-29:10:5.summary: “Blessed be the Lord’s glory” shares only the blessing formula.

1-chronicles-29:10:6.summary: A prayer naming “God our Father” shares only the Father title.

1-chronicles-29:10:7.summary: Glory “to our God and Father… for the ages of ages” echoes “our Father, from everlasting to everlasting.”

1-chronicles-29:10:8.summary: “Our Father” in the Lord’s Prayer shares the address of God as Father.
1-chronicles-29:10:8.why: Jesus’ use of the Father address.

1-chronicles-29:10:9.summary: A petition for daily bread has no link to David’s blessing.

1-chronicles-29:10:10.summary: “Thou, Lord, art our Father” is a rare Old Testament address matching “O Lord… our Father.”

1-chronicles-29:10:11.summary: Praising the Lord lifelong shares only general praise.

1-chronicles-29:10:12.summary: Crying “Abba, Father” shares the address of God as Father.

1-chronicles-29:10:13.summary: Jacob’s renaming as Israel shares only the name Israel.

1-chronicles-29:10:14.summary: “Blessed be the Lord for ever” matches the blessing of the Lord from everlasting to everlasting.

1-chronicles-29:10:15.summary: “Blessed be the Lord God, the God of Israel… for the age” closely matches David’s blessing.

1-chronicles-29:10:16.summary: “Bless the Lord, my soul” shares the act of blessing God.

1-chronicles-29:10:17.summary: Jacob calling on “the God of Israel” at an altar shares only the title.

1-chronicles-29:10:18.summary: Thanking the Lord with all the heart shares only general praise.

1-chronicles-29:10:19.summary: Solomon begins “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel,” the same blessing his father spoke.

1-chronicles-29:10:20.summary: “Blessed be the Lord, Israel’s God” repeats the blessing formula at the temple dedication.

1-chronicles-29:10:21.summary: In the same scene David calls the assembly to “Bless the Lord,” and they do.

1-chronicles-29:10:22.summary: The people bless the Lord in the Vale of Blessing, a general parallel.

1-chronicles-29:10:23.summary: “Bless the God of all” shares only the call to bless God.

1-chronicles-29:11:0.summary: Glory and “the word of His power” upholding all things loosely relate to God’s glory and rule.

1-chronicles-29:11:1.summary: Honor and glory to “the King of the ages” loosely echoes the doxology.

1-chronicles-29:11:2.summary: Nebuchadnezzar is told to give glory to the Most High, a general theme of God’s sovereignty.

1-chronicles-29:11:3.summary: Heaven and earth ascribe “power… strength and honour and glory” and dominion to God, echoing David’s list.

1-chronicles-29:11:4.summary: “Glory, majesty, might, and authority” to God parallels “greatness, power, glory… and strength.”

1-chronicles-29:11:5.summary: Proclaiming God’s exalted name among nations shares general praise.

1-chronicles-29:11:6.summary: God made the earth by His strength and gives it to whom He wills, a general sovereignty theme.

1-chronicles-29:11:7.summary: The kingdom of the world becoming the Lord’s shares the theme of God’s reign.

1-chronicles-29:11:8.summary: God exalted among nations and in the earth shares general sovereignty.

1-chronicles-29:11:9.summary: Angels ascribe “blessing and the glory and the wisdom… and the honour” to God, a heavenly doxology like David’s (truncated).

1-chronicles-29:11:10.summary: “To receive the glory and the honour and the power, because Thou didst create all things” parallels David’s ascription.

1-chronicles-29:11:11.summary: Nebuchadnezzar confesses God’s “everlasting kingship,” a general sovereignty theme.

1-chronicles-29:11:12.summary: “The glory and the power belong to our God” echoes “Thine… are… power, glory.”

1-chronicles-29:11:13.summary: God made heaven and earth, sharing only the heaven-and-earth scope.

1-chronicles-29:11:14.summary: “The Lord has become King! Let peoples be angry… let the earth be shaken” matches nations shaken before God’s rule.

1-chronicles-29:11:15.summary: Exalting “my God, my King” shares general praise of God’s kingship.

1-chronicles-29:11:16.summary: “Heaven is My throne, and earth the footstool” shares the heaven-and-earth sovereignty theme.
1-chronicles-29:11:16.why: God’s rule over heaven and earth.

1-chronicles-29:11:17.summary: The Lord’s voice “in strength… in magnificence” shares only general attributes.

1-chronicles-29:11:18.summary: The “only Sovereign… King of those who reign” with honor and might loosely echoes the doxology.

1-chronicles-29:11:19.summary: “Be exalted, Lord, in Thy power” shares general praise of God’s power.

1-chronicles-29:11:20.summary: The Lord made the earth by strength and wisdom, a general creator theme.

1-chronicles-29:11:21.summary: “The Lord has become King! Let the earth exult” shares the theme of God’s reign.

1-chronicles-29:11:22.summary: God made heaven and established the earth, a general creator theme.

1-chronicles-29:11:23.summary: “Thy might and the glory of the magnificence of Thy kingdom” closely parallels David’s ascription of might, glory, and rule.

1-chronicles-29:11:24.summary: The glory of the Lord’s strength makes the earth tremble, loosely like nations shaken.

1-chronicles-29:11:25.summary: The Almighty’s “great glory and honor” shares only general attributes.

1-chronicles-29:11:26.summary: The Saints psalm addresses a mighty king’s fairness and beauty, not God’s greatness and glory.

1-chronicles-29:11:27.summary: “Thou hast become very great… clothed… in praise and dignity” shares the greatness theme.

1-chronicles-29:11:28.summary: The Saints text speaks of God not changing His mind and lacks the divine title the link assumes.

1-chronicles-29:11:29.summary: God’s right hand winning salvation shares the victory theme generally.

1-chronicles-29:11:30.summary: God exalted above heavens and earth shares the heaven-and-earth sovereignty theme.

1-chronicles-29:11:31.summary: The Lord “Most High over all the earth” shares the sovereignty theme.

1-chronicles-29:11:32.summary: God exalted above heavens and earth shares the heaven-and-earth sovereignty theme.

1-chronicles-29:11:33.summary: God Most High “who created the heaven and the earth” shares the heaven-and-earth scope.
1-chronicles-29:11:33.why: God as owner of heaven and earth.

1-chronicles-29:11:34.summary: The mighty of the earth belong to God, a general sovereignty theme.

1-chronicles-29:11:35.summary: “Bless the Lord… from everlasting to everlasting” echoes the surrounding blessing, not this verse’s list.

1-chronicles-29:11:36.summary: God Most High who created heaven and earth shares the heaven-and-earth scope.

1-chronicles-29:11:37.summary: Heaven belongs to the Lord and the Lord made earth, a general ownership theme.

1-chronicles-29:11:38.summary: The Saints Matthew 6:13 lacks the closing doxology, so no kingdom-power-glory echo remains.
1-chronicles-29:11:38.why: Link depends on a textual variant.

1-chronicles-29:11:39.summary: Nebuchadnezzar’s humbling sentence shares no specific element with the doxology.

1-chronicles-29:11:40.summary: Nebuchadnezzar claims “my might… my glory,” the opposite of ascribing might and glory to God.

1-chronicles-29:12:0.summary: Being strengthened “according to the riches of His glory” loosely echoes God giving strength.

1-chronicles-29:12:1.summary: God “gives you strength to gain wealth,” matching wealth and strength coming from God.

1-chronicles-29:12:2.summary: “Thou rulest over all… In Thy hand is mighty strength” closely matches David’s words.

1-chronicles-29:12:3.summary: “Strength for all things in the One who empowers me” shares the strength-from-God theme.

1-chronicles-29:12:4.summary: Darius’ decree on God’s endurance shares no specific element.

1-chronicles-29:12:5.summary: Empowered “according to the might of His glory” shares the strength-from-God theme.

1-chronicles-29:12:6.summary: “From Him… are all things” loosely matches wealth and glory coming from God.

1-chronicles-29:12:7.summary: God able to do far more than we ask shares only the power theme.

1-chronicles-29:12:8.summary: God gives Solomon “wealth, possessions, and glory,” showing wealth and glory coming from God.

1-chronicles-29:12:9.summary: God “gives strength” shares only the general theme.

1-chronicles-29:12:10.summary: God has given wealth and possessions as His gift, sharing the theme of wealth from God.

1-chronicles-29:12:11.summary: God “humbles this one and raises that one,” loosely like God making great.

1-chronicles-29:12:12.summary: The Lord’s blessing “makes rich,” sharing the theme of wealth from God.

1-chronicles-29:12:13.summary: “The God of Israel will give power and strengthening to His people” matches God making great and strong.
1-chronicles-29:12:13.why: God gives strength to His people.

1-chronicles-29:12:14.summary: God raises the poor to sit with rulers, loosely like God making people great.

1-chronicles-29:12:15.summary: “Lord God Almighty… taken Thy great power and reigned” shares the Almighty-rules theme.

1-chronicles-29:12:16.summary: “He prevails in strength” shares only the strength theme.

1-chronicles-29:12:17.summary: “Righteousness and glory will come to Him” shares only the word glory.

1-chronicles-29:12:18.summary: “No one rescues from My hands” loosely matches power in God’s hand.

1-chronicles-29:12:19.summary: Wisdom says “Wealth and glory belong to me,” sharing the phrase but a different speaker.

1-chronicles-29:12:20.summary: “All authority in heaven and upon earth” loosely echoes God ruling all.

1-chronicles-29:12:21.summary: David blesses the Lord who trains and subjects peoples, sharing the strength theme.

1-chronicles-29:12:22.summary: God brings rulers down and raises the lowly, sharing the theme of God’s power over rank.

1-chronicles-29:12:23.summary: God’s counsel will stand shares only the sovereignty theme.

1-chronicles-29:12:24.summary: The shown verse says only “God spoke once; these two things I heard,” with no link.
1-chronicles-29:12:24.why: No real connection in shown text.

1-chronicles-29:12:25.summary: “Bring to the Lord glory and honor” shares only general praise.

1-chronicles-29:12:26.summary: The Lord as stronghold of His people shares only the strength theme.

1-chronicles-29:12:28.summary: “The Lord makes poor and makes rich; He humbles and raises high” matches wealth and greatness coming from God.

1-chronicles-29:12:29.summary: God doubles Job’s possessions, an example of wealth given by God.

1-chronicles-29:12:30.summary: “The Lord will give strength to His people” matches God making all strong.
1-chronicles-29:12:30.why: God gives strength to His people.

1-chronicles-29:12:31.summary: “God girds me with power” shares the strength-from-God theme.

1-chronicles-29:12:32.summary: God shows strength to whole hearts, sharing the strength theme.

1-chronicles-29:12:33.summary: Authority “given you from above” loosely matches all rule coming from God.

1-chronicles-29:13:0.summary: “Thanks be to God” shares only general thanksgiving.

1-chronicles-29:13:1.summary: “Give thanks to the Lord” shares only general thanksgiving.

1-chronicles-29:13:2.summary: “To Thee… I give thanks and praise” closely matches “we give thanks unto Thee, and praise.”

1-chronicles-29:13:3.summary: “Thanks be to God” shares only general thanksgiving.

1-chronicles-29:13:4.summary: “Give thanks to the Lord and call upon His name” shares thanks and the divine name.

1-chronicles-29:13:5.summary: “Thanks be to God” shares only general thanksgiving.

1-chronicles-29:13:6.summary: “We also thank God unceasingly” shares only general thanksgiving.

1-chronicles-29:14:0.summary: “Every complete gift is from above” matches “All things are Thine, and of Thine own have we given.”

1-chronicles-29:14:1.summary: “Our sufficiency is from God” loosely matches David’s humility about having strength to give.

1-chronicles-29:14:2.summary: “From Him and through Him and to Him are all things” matches “All things are Thine.”
1-chronicles-29:14:2.why: Pauline statement of the same truth.

1-chronicles-29:14:3.summary: Power made complete in weakness loosely echoes David’s “Who am I.”

1-chronicles-29:14:4.summary: God says the animals and “the inhabited world and its fullness are Mine,” matching “All things are Thine.”

1-chronicles-29:14:5.summary: “Not to us, Lord… but to Thy name give glory” shares the humility theme.
1-chronicles-29:14:5.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

1-chronicles-29:14:6.summary: The people “offered eagerly to the Lord,” the willing offering David marvels at.

1-chronicles-29:14:7.summary: “By God’s grace I am what I am” shares the humility theme.

1-chronicles-29:14:8.summary: God working in us “to will and to work” loosely matches strength to offer willingly.

1-chronicles-29:14:9.summary: Jacob’s humble acknowledgment of God’s goodness shares the humility theme.

1-chronicles-29:14:10.summary: David says “Who am I… and what is my house,” the same humble question.

1-chronicles-29:14:11.summary: “Of all that Thou givest me I will surely give a tenth to Thee” matches giving back from God’s own.

1-chronicles-29:14:12.summary: Nebuchadnezzar credits his own might, opposite to David crediting God.

1-chronicles-29:14:13.summary: Elders casting crowns before the throne loosely matches returning all to God.

1-chronicles-29:15:1.summary: “His days pass like a shadow” matches “our days upon earth are as a shadow.”

1-chronicles-29:15:2.summary: “My days bent like a shadow” matches days as a shadow.

1-chronicles-29:15:3.summary: Man “fled like a shadow and will not remain,” matching shadow and “no endurance.”

1-chronicles-29:15:4.summary: Life as a passing vapor shares the brevity theme with a different image.

1-chronicles-29:15:5.summary: “I am a sojourner with Thee and a temporary resident like all my fathers” closely matches David’s words.

1-chronicles-29:15:6.summary: All flesh as withering grass shares the brevity theme.

1-chronicles-29:15:7.summary: “I am a sojourner on the earth” matches being sojourners before God.

1-chronicles-29:15:8.summary: “All our days failed” shares the brevity theme.

1-chronicles-29:15:9.summary: The fathers confessed they were “strangers and sojourners upon the earth,” as David says.
1-chronicles-29:15:9.why: Heavenly hope behind the sojourner theme.

1-chronicles-29:15:10.summary: The days of life are spent “in a shadow,” matching days as a shadow.

1-chronicles-29:15:11.summary: Jacob speaks of his few days and the days his fathers “sojourned,” paralleling sojourners like the fathers.

1-chronicles-29:15:12.summary: Believers are addressed “as aliens and sojourners,” echoing David’s confession.

1-chronicles-29:15:13.summary: “All those things passed like a shadow” matches the shadow image of passing life.

1-chronicles-29:16:0.summary: David’s own words “All things are Thine, and of Thine own have we given” state the same truth.

1-chronicles-29:16:1.summary: “The earth and its fullness belong to the Lord” matches “everything is Thine.”

1-chronicles-29:16:2.summary: Israel did not know God gave her silver and gold, the opposite of David acknowledging all is from God.

1-chronicles-29:16:3.summary: Abundant offerings in the Lord’s house because the Lord blessed share the abundance theme.

1-chronicles-29:16:4.summary: A servant returning gain on the master’s mina loosely relates to giving back what is God’s.

1-chronicles-29:17:0.summary: Both affirm that the Lord himself “examines hearts”, the very confession David makes before the offering.
1-chronicles-29:17:0.why: Shows God's heart-searching as a recurring biblical confession.
1-chronicles-29:17:0.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

1-chronicles-29:17:1.summary: The Lord's delight in the blameless loosely matches David's integrity of heart, but there is no shared wording or setting.
1-chronicles-29:17:1.why: General background on God accepting the upright.

1-chronicles-29:17:3.summary: God's love of “truth” in the psalm loosely parallels His loving righteousness, but the context of repentance differs.
1-chronicles-29:17:3.why: Broad echo of what God loves in the inner person.

1-chronicles-29:17:4.summary: Paul appeals to God as witness of blameless conduct, a loose parallel to David's sincere giving before God.
1-chronicles-29:17:4.why: General theme of integrity under God's gaze.

1-chronicles-29:17:5.summary: God's word judging “the thoughts and intentions of the heart” touches the heart-examining theme only generally.
1-chronicles-29:17:5.why: Broad New Testament echo of divine heart-searching.

1-chronicles-29:17:7.summary: Nathanael's lack of deceit loosely resembles David's “simplicity of heart”, but nothing else connects the passages.

1-chronicles-29:17:8.summary: Refreshed hearts and joy among the saints share only incidental words with David's prayer about God testing hearts.
1-chronicles-29:17:8.why: No real link to the offering or heart-testing.

1-chronicles-29:17:9.summary: Paul's conduct “in simplicity and sincerity” before God echoes David's offering “in simplicity of heart”.
1-chronicles-29:17:9.why: Pairs two testimonies of sincere motive before God.

1-chronicles-29:17:10.summary: Paul's request to refresh his heart has no specific connection to David's prayer about examined hearts and willing gifts.

1-chronicles-29:17:11.summary: God testing Israel so “the things in your heart might be known” parallels David's confession that God examines hearts.
1-chronicles-29:17:11.why: Shows God's purpose in testing the heart.

1-chronicles-29:17:12.summary: The Lord “loves those who pursue righteousness” and accepts the upright's offerings, echoing David's “lovest righteousness” and sincere gifts.
1-chronicles-29:17:12.why: Links acceptable offering with an upright heart.

1-chronicles-29:17:13.summary: The psalm names “God who tests hearts and kidneys”, matching David's confession that God examines hearts.

1-chronicles-29:17:14.summary: Walking blamelessly and working righteousness with truth in the heart loosely matches David's sincere righteousness.
1-chronicles-29:17:14.why: General portrait of the upright worshipper.

1-chronicles-29:17:15.summary: Same occasion: the people “offered eagerly to the Lord with a full heart” and rejoiced, as David describes here.

1-chronicles-29:17:16.summary: The Greek proverb says the works of the humble are manifest before God, a loose echo of God seeing hearts.
1-chronicles-29:17:16.why: General idea of God seeing human deeds.

1-chronicles-29:17:17.summary: Paul's striving for a blameless conscience before God loosely parallels David's sincerity, with no shared wording.
1-chronicles-29:17:17.why: Broad theme of integrity before God.

1-chronicles-29:17:18.summary: Hearts tested like silver and gold before the Lord matches David's “Thou examinest hearts” amid gifts of gold and silver.
1-chronicles-29:17:18.why: Vivid image of God testing hearts.

1-chronicles-29:17:19.summary: The Greek proverb says the Lord sets hearts straight; it touches God's dealings with hearts but not examination or righteousness directly.
1-chronicles-29:17:19.why: Loose parallel on God's role over the heart.

1-chronicles-29:17:20.summary: Christ is “the One who searcheth kidneys and hearts”, the same divine attribute David confesses.
1-chronicles-29:17:20.why: Shows the attribute applied to Christ.

1-chronicles-29:17:21.summary: Wisdom's “love righteousness” and seeking God “in simplicity of heart” closely echo David's words here.
1-chronicles-29:17:21.why: Close verbal echo of David's sincerity language.

1-chronicles-29:18:0.summary: God promises to give “another heart, to fear Me always”, answering the kind of prayer David makes for lasting devotion.
1-chronicles-29:18:0.why: Shows God promising what David asks.

1-chronicles-29:18:1.summary: Man cannot direct his own course, implying God must; the link to David's prayer to direct hearts is indirect.
1-chronicles-29:18:1.why: Background on human dependence on God's direction.

1-chronicles-29:18:3.summary: Paul prays God will “encourage your hearts and establish them”, a loose parallel to David's prayer for the people's hearts.

1-chronicles-29:18:4.summary: A prayer for a clean heart shares the theme of God shaping the heart, but is personal repentance, not intercession.
1-chronicles-29:18:4.why: General parallel of praying for a renewed heart.

1-chronicles-29:18:5.summary: God working in believers what pleases Him loosely parallels David asking God to direct hearts toward Him.
1-chronicles-29:18:5.why: Broad theme of God enabling obedience.

1-chronicles-29:18:6.summary: Paul asks God to “direct our way”, sharing the verb but concerning travel, not hearts.
1-chronicles-29:18:6.why: Verbal echo of a directing prayer.

1-chronicles-29:18:7.summary: Loving God's law and hating lawbreakers has no specific connection to David's prayer for the people's hearts.
1-chronicles-29:18:7.why: No shared element beyond general devotion.

1-chronicles-29:18:8.summary: God attending to “the preparation of their heart” loosely relates to David asking God to direct hearts.
1-chronicles-29:18:8.why: Loose echo of God's involvement with hearts.

1-chronicles-29:18:9.summary: Awaiting salvation and loving commandments shares nothing specific with David's prayer to keep the people's hearts.

1-chronicles-29:18:10.summary: Both invoke “the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob”, the God of the fathers.

1-chronicles-29:18:11.summary: The Lord cleansing the heart of the people and their seed relates loosely to David's prayer to direct hearts.
1-chronicles-29:18:11.why: Background on God transforming Israel's heart.

1-chronicles-29:18:12.summary: God names Himself “the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob”, the title David invokes.
1-chronicles-29:18:12.why: Origin of the ancestral title used in prayer.

1-chronicles-29:18:13.summary: Jesus quotes the patriarchal divine title, matching David's address only in that formula.
1-chronicles-29:18:13.why: Shows the same title in a different argument.

1-chronicles-29:18:14.summary: Confidence that God will complete His work in believers loosely parallels David asking God to preserve the people's devotion.
1-chronicles-29:18:14.why: General theme of God sustaining faithfulness.

1-chronicles-29:18:15.summary: “The God of your fathers, the God of Abraham… Isaac… Jacob” matches David's invocation and is called God's everlasting name.
1-chronicles-29:18:15.why: Shows the covenant name David appeals to.

1-chronicles-29:18:16.summary: Humanity setting its heart continually on evil contrasts with David's prayer that hearts be kept toward God.
1-chronicles-29:18:16.why: Shows why the heart needs God's direction.

1-chronicles-29:18:17.summary: Paul's prayer for believers' discernment and purity is a general parallel to David's intercession for the people.
1-chronicles-29:18:17.why: Comparable intercessory prayer for God's people.

1-chronicles-29:18:18.summary: Peter invokes “the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, the God of our fathers”, David's same address.
1-chronicles-29:18:18.why: Shows continuity of the ancestral title.

1-chronicles-29:19:0.summary: David charges “Solomon my son” to serve God with a whole heart, the same concern he prays for here.
1-chronicles-29:19:0.why: David's charge matches his prayer for Solomon.

1-chronicles-29:19:1.summary: A psalm “for Solomon” asks God to give the king's son righteousness, paralleling David's prayer for Solomon's heart.
1-chronicles-29:19:1.why: Another prayer for Solomon's godly rule.

1-chronicles-29:19:2.summary: Every good gift coming from above shares only the idea of God giving, not David's specific prayer for Solomon.

1-chronicles-29:19:3.summary: “Let my heart be blameless in Thine ordinances” mirrors David's request for a good heart to keep God's ordinances.
1-chronicles-29:19:3.why: Parallel prayer for a heart obedient to God's statutes.

1-chronicles-29:19:4.summary: David's preparation of gold, silver, and materials for the Lord's house is the work he prays Solomon will complete.
1-chronicles-29:19:4.why: Shows what Solomon was to finish.

1-chronicles-29:19:5.summary: Same speech: David calls “Solomon my son” young for the great building work he has prepared.

1-chronicles-29:20:0.summary: The call to “bow down and fall before Him” matches the assembly's prostration only as a general worship posture.

1-chronicles-29:20:1.summary: The people bowing and worshipping at God's visitation is a general parallel to the assembly's prostration.

1-chronicles-29:20:2.summary: A Davidic psalm of blessing God's name shares the theme of blessing the Lord; judged on the shown truncated text.

1-chronicles-29:20:3.summary: Under David, “Blessed be the Lord, Israel's God” is spoken and all the people praise, as the assembly does here.
1-chronicles-29:20:3.why: Earlier Davidic assembly blessing the Lord.

1-chronicles-29:20:4.summary: A call for Israel to praise the Lord's name parallels the assembly's blessing only in general terms.
1-chronicles-29:20:4.why: General theme of Israel praising God.

1-chronicles-29:20:5.summary: The imperative “bless the Lord” echoes David's call, but the setting is night temple worship.
1-chronicles-29:20:5.why: Same liturgical call in a different setting.

1-chronicles-29:20:6.summary: “Fear God, son, and the king” pairs reverence for God and king, as the assembly prostrates before both.
1-chronicles-29:20:6.why: Explains honor given to God and king together.

1-chronicles-29:20:7.summary: Jehoshaphat appoints singers to praise the Lord, a general parallel to corporate worship led by a king.
1-chronicles-29:20:7.why: Another king leading the people in praise.

1-chronicles-29:20:8.summary: “Fear God. Honor the king.” pairs reverence for God and the king, as in the assembly's double prostration.
1-chronicles-29:20:8.why: New Testament pairing of God and king.

1-chronicles-29:20:9.summary: The servant “worshipped the Lord, and blessed the Lord, the God of my master Abraham”, closely matching the assembly's acts.
1-chronicles-29:20:9.why: Shows the same pairing of worship and blessing.

1-chronicles-29:20:10.summary: “All the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel” parallels reverence given to the Lord and His appointed leader together.
1-chronicles-29:20:10.why: Comparable honor to God and His leader.

1-chronicles-29:20:11.summary: A man worshipping the Lord shares only the general act of worship with the assembly's prostration.

1-chronicles-29:20:12.summary: Repeated calls to “bless the Lord” echo David's summons, but in a different liturgical setting.
1-chronicles-29:20:12.why: Liturgical parallel to the call to bless.

1-chronicles-29:20:13.summary: The people fearing the Lord and trusting Moses loosely parallels honoring God and His leader, but no worship act is shared.
1-chronicles-29:20:13.why: Loose parallel of God and leader honored.

1-chronicles-29:20:14.summary: A Davidic call to “bow down to the Lord” shares only a general worship theme.

1-chronicles-29:20:15.summary: Israel “blessed the God of the sons of Israel” after a dispute, a loose parallel to the assembly blessing God.

1-chronicles-29:21:0.summary: Large numbers of bulls, rams, and lambs offered for all Israel at the house's dedication parallel David's lavish sacrifices.
1-chronicles-29:21:0.why: Comparable national sacrifice at a temple milestone.

1-chronicles-29:21:1.summary: Solomon's massive sacrifices of calves and flocks with all the people parallel David's thousandfold offerings; shown text only.
1-chronicles-29:21:1.why: Follows the pattern into Solomon's dedication.

1-chronicles-29:21:2.summary: Rules for wine drink offerings relate only to the “libations” mentioned with David's sacrifices.

1-chronicles-29:21:3.summary: A prescribed drink offering of wine relates only generally to the libations accompanying David's sacrifices.

1-chronicles-29:21:4.summary: Wine prepared as a drink offering for each lamb loosely explains the lambs “with their libations”.

1-chronicles-29:21:5.summary: Half a hin of wine as drink offering gives only general background to the libations mentioned.

1-chronicles-29:21:6.summary: Solomon and all Israel offering enormous numbers of cattle and sheep closely parallels David's mass sacrifices for all Israel.

1-chronicles-29:22:0.summary: Solomon appoints Zadok priest in Abiathar's place, matching Sadok's anointing for priesthood here.

1-chronicles-29:22:3.summary: Israel's leaders “ate and drank” in God's presence, like the people eating and drinking “before the Lord”.
1-chronicles-29:22:3.why: Shows sacred meals in God's presence.

1-chronicles-29:22:4.summary: The people eating and drinking with great gladness parallels the festive joy only in general terms.

1-chronicles-29:22:5.summary: Eating and drinking with gladness shares a general motif but has no cultic or royal setting.

1-chronicles-29:22:6.summary: Instructions to the rich about generosity have no specific link to the feast and Solomon's anointing.

1-chronicles-29:22:7.summary: Bathsheba's homage belongs to Solomon's first accession story, which the “second time” alludes to, but the verse itself is about David.

1-chronicles-29:22:8.summary: Praise of eating, drinking, and rejoicing is a general motif without the worship setting.
1-chronicles-29:22:8.why: General motif of joy in God's gifts.

1-chronicles-29:22:9.summary: Bringing offerings to God's chosen place and rejoicing before Him matches the people's sacrifices and joyful feast.
1-chronicles-29:22:9.why: Shows the law behind joyful sacrificial feasts.

1-chronicles-29:22:10.summary: Eating and drinking as God's gift loosely parallels the feast's joy.
1-chronicles-29:22:10.why: General motif of joy in eating.

1-chronicles-29:22:11.summary: People rejoicing with a good heart over the Lord's goodness to David and Solomon parallels this joyful accession feast.

1-chronicles-29:22:12.summary: “You shall eat there before the Lord your God, and rejoice” matches eating and drinking “before the Lord… with joy”.
1-chronicles-29:22:12.why: Legal pattern for rejoicing before God.

1-chronicles-29:22:13.summary: Eating and drinking as from God's hand shares only a general motif with the feast.

1-chronicles-29:22:14.summary: Rejoicing at the feasts before the Lord loosely parallels this festive gathering; shown text only.

1-chronicles-29:23:1.summary: God chose Solomon “to seat him upon the throne”, fulfilled as Solomon sits on David's throne here.
1-chronicles-29:23:1.why: Shows the choice behind the enthronement.

1-chronicles-29:23:2.summary: Submitting to God-appointed authorities loosely relates to all Israel obeying Solomon.
1-chronicles-29:23:2.why: General teaching on obedience to rulers.

1-chronicles-29:23:3.summary: Advice to keep the king's command relates loosely to Israel obeying Solomon.

1-chronicles-29:23:4.summary: David's promise that the Lord would grant Solomon success is realized as Solomon is accepted with favor.

1-chronicles-29:23:5.summary: A ruler “upon the throne of David” shares the throne motif but concerns a future messianic king.
1-chronicles-29:23:5.why: Extends the throne of David theme.

1-chronicles-29:23:6.summary: God's oath to set David's offspring “on your throne” is fulfilled as Solomon sits on David's throne.

1-chronicles-29:23:7.summary: God's promise to raise David's offspring and establish his throne is realized in Solomon's enthronement.
1-chronicles-29:23:7.why: Links accession to the Davidic covenant.

1-chronicles-29:24:0.summary: David tells Solomon the rulers and all the people are ready for his words, anticipating their submission here.
1-chronicles-29:24:0.why: Shows the leaders' readiness to serve Solomon.

1-chronicles-29:24:1.summary: David commands all Israel's rulers to support Solomon, matching their submission to him here.
1-chronicles-29:24:1.why: Background command for the rulers' support.

1-chronicles-29:24:2.summary: Solomon's execution of Adonijah concerns consolidating David's throne, but shows enforcement rather than willing submission of David's sons.

1-chronicles-29:24:3.summary: The Saints text calls for serving the Lord and entering His sanctuary; nothing parallels submission to Solomon.
1-chronicles-29:24:3.why: The assumed “give the hand” idiom is absent.
1-chronicles-29:24:3.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

1-chronicles-29:24:4.summary: Abraham's servant placing a hand under his thigh shares nothing with the rulers submitting to Solomon in this wording.
1-chronicles-29:24:4.why: Hand-pledge idiom not present in source.

1-chronicles-29:24:5.summary: A broken oath of allegiance in Ezekiel shares only the idea of pledging, not present in the source's “submitted”.
1-chronicles-29:24:5.why: Link depends on a Hebrew idiom absent here.

1-chronicles-29:24:6.summary: Adonijah, a son of David, prostrates himself before King Solomon, an instance of David's sons submitting to him.
1-chronicles-29:24:6.why: Concrete case of a rival brother submitting.

1-chronicles-29:24:7.summary: Jacob's request to Joseph about burial has no connection to the rulers' submission to Solomon.
1-chronicles-29:24:7.why: No shared person, event, or wording.

1-chronicles-29:24:8.summary: Judah's genealogy shares nothing specific with the rulers and David's sons submitting to Solomon.

1-chronicles-29:25:0.summary: God promises Solomon glory such that none like him existed “among the kings before you”, matching this verse.
1-chronicles-29:25:0.why: Promise fulfilled in Solomon's unrivaled glory.

1-chronicles-29:25:1.summary: The Lord “made him exceedingly great” repeats this verse's description of Solomon.
1-chronicles-29:25:1.why: Chronicler's parallel opening of Solomon's reign.

1-chronicles-29:25:3.summary: The Preacher “grew great and surpassed everyone who was before me in Jerusalem”, echoing Solomon's unmatched greatness.
1-chronicles-29:25:3.why: Solomonic voice reflecting the same greatness.

1-chronicles-29:25:4.summary: The Lord begins to exalt Joshua “before all the sons of Israel”, as He makes Solomon great before all Israel.
1-chronicles-29:25:4.why: Pattern of God exalting a successor.

1-chronicles-29:25:5.summary: The name of Jesus being magnified in Ephesus shares only the idea of magnifying, not Solomon's royal glory.

1-chronicles-29:25:6.summary: Job's question why God magnifies a human being is unrelated to Solomon's exaltation as king.

1-chronicles-29:25:8.summary: “The Lord exalted Joshua before the whole race of Israel” parallels God making Solomon great before all Israel.
1-chronicles-29:25:8.why: Similar divine exaltation of a successor.

1-chronicles-29:25:9.summary: Jesus crowned with glory through suffering shares only the word glory with Solomon's royal honor.

1-chronicles-29:26:0.summary: “David reigned over all Israel” restates this summary of David's reign.

1-chronicles-29:26:1.summary: God took David to shepherd Israel His inheritance, describing the same reign over Israel.

1-chronicles-29:27:2.summary: Both give David's reign as seven years in Hebron/Chebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.
1-chronicles-29:27:2.why: Parallel chronology, noting the extra six months.

1-chronicles-29:28:4.summary: Abraham “died in a good old age… full of days”, the same formula used of David.
1-chronicles-29:28:4.why: Places David among blessed patriarchal deaths.

1-chronicles-29:28:0.summary: The promise of burial “at a good old age” uses the same phrase as David's death notice.
1-chronicles-29:28:0.why: Shows the blessing of a good old age.

1-chronicles-29:28:1.summary: Paul recounts that David, having served his generation, fell asleep and was gathered to his fathers.
1-chronicles-29:28:1.why: New Testament reflection on David's death.

1-chronicles-29:28:2.summary: Coming to the grave like ripe grain at its season loosely parallels dying in a good old age.
1-chronicles-29:28:2.why: Image of a timely, full death.

1-chronicles-29:28:3.summary: David “old and full of days” made Solomon king in his place, matching this verse's wording and succession.
1-chronicles-29:28:3.why: Earlier notice of the same succession.

1-chronicles-29:28:5.summary: Isaac died “old and full of days”, the same formula applied to David.

1-chronicles-29:28:6.summary: Old age as a crown found in righteousness loosely relates to David's honored old age.
1-chronicles-29:28:6.why: General wisdom on honorable old age.

1-chronicles-29:29:0.summary: Explains that a prophet was formerly called “the seer”, the title given Samuel and Gad here.

1-chronicles-29:29:1.summary: “Nathan the prophet” confronts David, the same Nathan whose records are cited; shown text only.
1-chronicles-29:29:1.why: Shows Nathan's role in David's story.

1-chronicles-29:29:2.summary: “Gad, David's seer” brings the Lord's word to David, the same Gad the seer cited here.
1-chronicles-29:29:2.why: Shows Gad's prophetic role with David.

1-chronicles-29:29:3.summary: David consults “Nathan the prophet”, the same prophet whose records are named.

1-chronicles-29:29:4.summary: “The prophet Gad” advises David, the same Gad whose records are cited.
1-chronicles-29:29:4.why: Earliest appearance of Gad with David.

1-chronicles-29:29:5.summary: Solomon's remaining acts are said to be written in a book, the same closing formula used for David.

1-chronicles-29:29:6.summary: Rehoboam's remaining acts are “written” in royal annals, matching the source-citation formula here.
1-chronicles-29:29:6.why: Same formula for citing royal records.

1-chronicles-29:29:7.summary: David, Samuel, and the prophets are named together, but only in a general list of faithful heroes.
1-chronicles-29:29:7.why: New Testament remembrance of David and Samuel.

1-chronicles-29:30:0.summary: The shown text on Nebuchadnezzar's tree vision does not mention “times”, so it shares nothing with David's records.
1-chronicles-29:30:0.why: The assumed link to “times” is absent.

1-chronicles-29:30:1.summary: Being led into custody in a deserted place has no connection to the summary of David's reign.
1-chronicles-29:30:1.why: No shared element in this wording.

1-chronicles-29:30:2.summary: Jehu's remaining acts and “all his power” are recorded, matching the formula about David's dominion and records.

1-chronicles-29:30:3.summary: Jeroboam's deeds and mighty acts are written in the chronicles, the same closing formula.

1-chronicles-29:30:4.summary: God “changes seasons and times” and appoints kings, loosely echoing the “times” over Israel and kingdoms.
1-chronicles-29:30:4.why: Theological frame for the times of kingdoms.

1-chronicles-29:12:27.summary: Daniel 5:18–21 has no corresponding passage in this edition, which follows the Greek text; there is no Saints reading to compare.
1-chronicles-29:12:27.why: Compare a Hebrew-based translation if this passage matters for study.
1-chronicles-29:12:27.note: Passage unavailable in this edition; the review records the absence rather than an interpretation.

1-chronicles-29:25:7.summary: Daniel 5:18–19 has no corresponding passage in this edition, which follows the Greek text; there is no Saints reading to compare.
1-chronicles-29:25:7.why: Compare a Hebrew-based translation if this passage matters for study.
1-chronicles-29:25:7.note: Passage unavailable in this edition; the review records the absence rather than an interpretation.
